SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p644/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p644/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p644/r1.claim: The author observes that Qur’anic إلى accompanies rational recipients, while على is used for both rational and inanimate recipients.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p644/r1.anchor: أما (على) فهي استعملت للعاقل وغير العاقل

STUDYQURAN:4:105/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:4:105/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:4:105/r1.claim: One purpose of revelation was to enable the Prophet to judge among people according to what God had taught him.
STUDYQURAN:4:105/r1.anchor: one of the purposes of the revelation to the Prophet was that he might judge between men according to what God has shown him—that is, according to what God has taught him (R).

STUDYQURAN:4:105/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:4:105/r2.speaker: Some scholars
STUDYQURAN:4:105/r2.claim: Some scholars cite this wording as evidence that the Prophet could perform ijtihād by deriving rulings from Quranic principles and laws.
STUDYQURAN:4:105/r2.anchor: Some scholars adduce this phrase to demonstrate that the Prophet had been given permission to perform ijtihād—that is, to derive independent rulings from the principles and laws contained in the Quran (IK).

STUDYQURAN:4:105/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:4:105/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:4:105/r3.claim: The verses reportedly concern Ṭuʿmah ibn Ubayriq, likely a hypocrite, who stole armor, hid it among a Madinan Jew’s belongings, and accused him; after relatives solicited the Prophet’s defense, revelation warned him and directed him to seek forgiveness.
STUDYQURAN:4:105/r3.anchor: at the behest of the latter’s relatives, but in v. 105 he was warned not to defend

STUDYQURAN:4:105/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:4:105/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:4:105/r4.claim: The parallel between betraying trusts and betraying oneself concerns the same people and reflects that moral actions ultimately affect the actor.
STUDYQURAN:4:105/r4.anchor: The parallelism between those who betray their trust in v. 105 and those who betray their own selves in v. 107, which both refer to the same people, reflects the Quranic idea that one’s moral or immoral actions ultimately affect only oneself (see v. 111).

STUDYQURAN:4:105/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:4:105/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:4:105/r5.claim: The Quran repeatedly says that God does not wrong people; people wrong themselves.
STUDYQURAN:4:105/r5.anchor: Hence the assertion found throughout the Quran in relation to wrongdoers that God does not wrong people, but that they wrong themselves (see, e.g., 2:57; 3:117; 7:160).

STUDYQURAN:4:105/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:4:105/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:4:105/r6.claim: The Prophet must apply Quranic rulings without favoritism, even when a nominal fellow Muslim is opposed to a member of another religious community.
STUDYQURAN:4:105/r6.anchor: The Prophet is instructed to apply the rulings of the Quran without favoritism toward anyone—even on behalf of a (perhaps nominal) fellow Muslim against a member of another religious community (R).

STUDYQURAN:4:105/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:4:105/r7.speaker: Some
STUDYQURAN:4:105/r7.claim: Some argue that the warnings and forgiveness command imply the Prophet initially intended to advocate for Ṭuʿmah, which would challenge the doctrine that prophets are protected from major sins.
STUDYQURAN:4:105/r7.anchor: a few have argued that these verses indicate that the Prophet was initially willing to advocate for the lying

STUDYQURAN:4:105/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:4:105/r8.speaker: al-Rāzī
STUDYQURAN:4:105/r8.claim: Al-Rāzī replies that the Prophet was concerned and willing to get involved but took no decisive action while awaiting revelation, so the report does not establish a sinful defense.
STUDYQURAN:4:105/r8.anchor: Al-Rāzī responds to this argument by noting that the report of this incident indicates that, although the Prophet was concerned about the situation and willing to get involved, he took no decisive action right away

TABATABAI:4:105-109/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:105-109/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:105-109/r1.claim: The passage forms one unit urging judicial justice and forbidding judges to favor wrongdoers over the rightful, while teaching that religion is a lived truth rather than a name.
TABATABAI:4:105-109/r1.anchor: أنها ذات سياق واحد تتعرض للتوصية بالعدل في القضاء

TABATABAI:4:105-109/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:105-109/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:105-109/r3.claim: Although betrayal often means breach of a trust, here the context points to theft and similar acts; because believers are like one self, violating another believer's property betrays the community.

TABATABAI:4:105-109/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:105-109/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:105-109/r4.claim: His reconstruction is that some people stole, accused an innocent person, and pressed the Prophet to judge for the thief and against the accused.
TABATABAI:4:105-109/r4.anchor: فالتدبر يقرب أن القصة كأنها سرقة وقعت من بعضهم ثم رفع الأمر إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم فرمى بها السارق غيره ممن هو بريء منها

TABATABAI:4:105-109/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:105-109/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:105-109/r5.claim: The passage fits the reported occasion about Abu Tuʿmah ibn al-Abyraq's theft, though al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī cautions that most occasion reports apply remembered stories to verses they resemble.
TABATABAI:4:105-109/r5.anchor: فالآيات أشد انطباقا على ما روي في سبب النزول من قصة سرقة أبي طعمة بن الأبيرق

TABATABAI:4:105-109/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:105-109/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:105-109/r6.claim: The verses establish the binding authority of the Prophet's judicial decisions.
TABATABAI:4:105-109/r6.anchor: ويستفاد من الآيات حجية قضائه صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

TABATABAI:4:105-109/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:105-109/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:105-109/r7.claim: The passage also establishes the Prophet's protection from error, alongside other religious truths to be discussed later.

TABATABAI:4:105-106/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:105-106/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:105-106/r1.claim: Verse 4:105 applies in a particular case what 2:213 states generally: God sent the Book to settle human disputes.

TABATABAI:4:105-106/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:105-106/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:105-106/r2.claim: Unlike the general statement in 2:213, this verse grants the Messenger the right to judge and makes his own judgment authoritative.
TABATABAI:4:105-106/r2.anchor: وتزيد عليها في أنها تدل على جعل حق الحكم لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم والحجية لرأيه ونظره

TABATABAI:4:105-106/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:105-106/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:105-106/r3.claim: Judging a concrete dispute requires the judge's own determination of which general rule applies; knowing the laws and rights alone does not settle the case.
TABATABAI:4:105-106/r3.anchor: فإن العلم بكليات الأحكام وحقوق الناس أمر

TABATABAI:4:105-106/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:105-106/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:105-106/r4.claim: The phrase means God formed the Prophet's judgment and disclosed the ruling to him, not merely that He taught him general laws, as some have suggested.

TABATABAI:4:105-106/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:105-106/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:105-106/r5.claim: God taught the Prophet the Book's rules and wisdom, then added the judgment He gave him so the Prophet could adjudicate and end disputes.
TABATABAI:4:105-106/r5.anchor: أن الله أنزل إليك الكتاب وعلمك أحكامه وشرائعه وحكمه لتضيف إليها ما أوجد لك من الرأي وعرفك من الحكم فتحكم بين الناس

TABATABAI:4:105-106/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:105-106/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:105-106/r6.claim: The prohibition is coordinated with the preceding declarative sentence, which functions as a command: judge among them and do not advocate for traitors.
TABATABAI:4:105-106/r6.anchor: عطف على ما تقدمه من الجملة الخبرية لكونها في معنى الإنشاء كأنه قيل فاحكم بينهم ولا تكن للخائنين خصيما

TABATABAI:4:105-106/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:105-106/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:105-106/r7.claim: A khasim is someone who defends a claim or its equivalent.
TABATABAI:4:105-106/r7.anchor: والخصيم هو الذي يدافع عن الدعوى وما في حكمها

TABATABAI:4:105-106/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:105-106/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:105-106/r8.claim: The Prophet is forbidden to defend traitors against people claiming their rights, thereby voiding the rightful party's claim.
TABATABAI:4:105-106/r8.anchor: وفيه نهيه صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم عن أن يكون خصيما للخائنين على من يطالبهم بحقوقه فيدافع عن الخائنين ويبطل حقوق المحقين

TABATABAI:4:105-106/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:105-106/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:105-106/r9.claim: The context suggests betrayal means any wrongful violation of another's rights, not only breach of entrusted deposits, though a specific case could sometimes be attached to a general rule.
TABATABAI:4:105-106/r9.anchor: أن المراد بالخيانة مطلق التعدي على حقوق الغير ممن لا ينبغي منه ذلك لا خصوص الخيانة للودائع

TABATABAI:4:105-126#2/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:105-126#2/r4.speaker: قتادة بن النعمان
TABATABAI:4:105-126#2/r4.claim: Al-Durr al-manthur cites a report from Qatada, authenticated by al-Hakim, about the Banu Ubayriq theft: Bashir wrote anti-Companion verse and passed it off on others; flour and weapons were stolen from Rifa'a.
TABATABAI:4:105-126#2/r4.anchor: وفي الدر المنثور أخرج الترمذي وابن جرير وابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم وأبو الشيخ والحاكم وصححه عن قتادة بن النعمان

TABATABAI:4:105-126#3/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:105-126#3/r1.speaker: قتادة بن النعمان
TABATABAI:4:105-126#3/r1.claim: Qatada recounts that the Banu Ubayriq enlisted Usayr ibn Urwa and neighbors to accuse him and Rifa'a of slandering a pious household; the Prophet challenged Qatada for alleging theft without proof.
TABATABAI:4:105-126#3/r1.anchor: قال قتادة فأتيت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فكلمته، فقال عمدت إلى أهل بيت ذكر منهم إسلام وصلاح

TABATABAI:4:105-126#3/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:105-126#3/r2.speaker: قتادة بن النعمان
TABATABAI:4:105-126#3/r2.claim: Qatada’s report glosses the “traitors” as the Banu Ubayriq, the command to seek forgiveness as concerning the Prophet’s rebuke of Qatada, the slander as their charge against Lubayd, and the party as Usayr ibn Urwa’s allies.
TABATABAI:4:105-126#3/r2.anchor: ولا تكن للخائنين خصيما - بني أبيرق - واستغفر الله - أي مما قلت لقتادة

TABATABAI:4:105-126#3/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:105-126#3/r3.speaker: قتادة بن النعمان
TABATABAI:4:105-126#3/r3.claim: After revelation exposed the theft, the Prophet returned the stolen weapons to Rifa'a; Qatada says his uncle then declared them a path devoted to God, confirming his Islam was sincere.
TABATABAI:4:105-126#3/r3.anchor: فلما نزل القرآن أتى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بالسلاح فرده إلى رفاعة

TABATABAI:4:105-126#4/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:105-126#4/r1.speaker: قتادة بن النعمان
TABATABAI:4:105-126#4/r1.claim: Qatada says Rifa'a's declaration that the returned weapon was for God convinced him that his uncle’s Islam was genuine; after the Qur'an exposed him, Bashir fled to Mecca.
TABATABAI:4:105-126#4/r1.anchor: قال قتادة فلما أتيت عمي بالسلاح، وكان شيخا قد عسا في الجاهلية وكنت أرى إسلامه مدخولا

TABATABAI:4:105-126#4/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:105-126#4/r3.speaker: ابن زيد
TABATABAI:4:105-126#4/r3.claim: Ibn Zayd gives a variant: a thief framed a Jewish man for stealing armor, whose neighbors defended the thief and disparaged the Jew; revelation rebuked their defense, offered repentance, and the thief later died when a house he tried to rob collapsed.
TABATABAI:4:105-126#4/r3.anchor: أخرج ابن جرير عن ابن زيد في الآية قال كان رجل سرق درعا من حديد

TABATABAI:4:105-126#4/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:105-126#4/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:105-126#4/r4.claim: Al-Tabataba'i says the same basic account is transmitted through many routes with only slight differences.
TABATABAI:4:105-126#4/r4.anchor: أقول وهذا المعنى أيضا مروي بطرق كثيرة مع اختلاف يسير فيها

TABRISI:4:105-106/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:105-106/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:4:105-106/r1.claim: The revelation is placed in the case of three Banū Ubairiq brothers: Bishr, Bashīr, and Mubashshir; Bashīr, called Abū Ṭuʿma, wrote satires against the Prophet’s companions and attributed them to others.
TABRISI:4:105-106/r1.anchor: نزلت في بني أبيرق وكانوا ثلاثة إخوة بشر وبشير ومبشر وكان بشير يكنى أبا طعمة

TABRISI:4:105-106/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:105-106/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:4:105-106/r2.claim: Abū Ṭuʿma broke into the upper room of Rifāʿa ibn Zayd and stole food, a sword, and armor; Rifāʿa complained to his nephew Qatāda ibn al-Nuʿmān.
TABRISI:4:105-106/r2.anchor: فنقب أبو طعمة على علية رفاعة بن زيد وأخذ له طعاما وسيفا ودرعا

TABRISI:4:105-106/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:105-106/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:4:105-106/r3.claim: When Qatāda and Rifāʿa investigated, the brothers blamed the theft on Labīd ibn Sahl; Labīd confronted them, accusing them of theft and hypocrisy and warning them to stop slandering the Prophet.
TABRISI:4:105-106/r3.anchor: فقال بنو أبيرق والله ما صاحبكم إلا لبيد بن سهل رجل ذو حسب ونسب

TABRISI:4:105-106/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:105-106/r4.speaker: قتادة بن النعمان
TABRISI:4:105-106/r4.claim: Qatāda told the Prophet that a bad household had attacked his uncle and broken into his upper room, taking food and weapons; the Prophet first told him to investigate.
TABRISI:4:105-106/r4.anchor: وأتى قتادة رسول الله فقال يا رسول الله إن أهل بيت منا أهل بيت سوء عدوا على عمي

TABRISI:4:105-106/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:105-106/r5.speaker: أسير بن عروة
TABRISI:4:105-106/r5.claim: Usayr ibn ʿUrwa gathered men from the brothers’ clan and accused Qatāda and Rifāʿa of slandering a reputable, righteous household; after hearing him, the Prophet rebuked Qatāda when he returned.
TABRISI:4:105-106/r5.anchor: يقال له أسير بن عروة جمع رجالا من أهل الدار ثم انطلق إلى رسول الله

TABRISI:4:105-106/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:105-106/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:4:105-106/r6.claim: Qatāda left wishing he had died rather than speak to the Prophet; Rifāʿa replied that God was the one to seek help from. The passage from this verse through “God does not forgive associating partners” was revealed.
TABRISI:4:105-106/r6.anchor: فقال عمه رفاعة الله المستعان فنزلت الآيات

TABRISI:4:105-106/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:105-106/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:4:105-106/r7.claim: When Bashīr learned that the Qurʾān had exposed him, he fled to Mecca and apostatized; he stayed with Sulāfa bt. Saʿd, whom Ḥassān satirized in a poem.
TABRISI:4:105-106/r7.anchor: فبلغ بشيرا ما نزل فيه من القرآن فهرب إلى مكة وارتد كافرا فنزل على سلافة بنت سعد

TABRISI:4:105-106#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:105-106#2/r1.speaker: مجاهد، قتادة بن النعمان، عكرمة، ابن جريج
TABRISI:4:105-106#2/r1.claim: These authorities relate the preceding incident: a woman carried the man's load on her head, cast it at al-Abṭaḥ, and complained that he had brought her nothing good, citing poetry by Ḥassān.
TABRISI:4:105-106#2/r1.anchor: هذا قول مجاهد وقتادة بن النعمان وعكرمة وابن جريج إلا أن عكرمة قال

TABRISI:4:105-106#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:105-106#2/r2.speaker: عكرمة وابن عباس
TABRISI:4:105-106#2/r2.claim: They say Banū Ubairiq planted the stolen property on a Jew, Zayd ibn al-Suhaym, and asked the Prophet to argue for them; he intended to do so and punish the Jew before revelation came.
TABRISI:4:105-106#2/r2.anchor: إن بني أبيرق طرحوا ذلك على يهودي يقال له: زيد بن السهين فجاء اليهودي إلى رسول الله

TABRISI:4:105-106#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:105-106#2/r3.speaker: الضحاك
TABRISI:4:105-106#2/r3.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says an Anṣārī who had entrusted armor was falsely accused of denying it; his clan sought the Prophet's support, and the verses came after the Prophet defended him as apparently innocent.
TABRISI:4:105-106#2/r3.anchor: وقال الضحاك: نزلت في رجل من الأنصار استودع درعا فجحد صاحبها

TABRISI:4:105-106#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:105-106#2/r4.speaker: الطبري
TABRISI:4:105-106#2/r4.claim: Al-Ṭabarī prefers the entrusted-armor account because betrayal properly concerns a deposit, whereas theft is not betrayal in this sense.
TABRISI:4:105-106#2/r4.anchor: واختار الطبري هذا الوجه قال لأن الخيانة إنما تكون في الوديعة لا في السرقة

TABRISI:4:105-106#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:105-106#2/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:4:105-106#2/r5.claim: God says He sent the Qur'an in truth, meaning with what God is due from His servants; another gloss is that Muḥammad is more entitled to it.

TABRISI:4:105-106#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:105-106#2/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:4:105-106#2/r6.claim: The Prophet is to judge among people by what God has shown him, that is, what God taught him in His Book.

TABRISI:4:105-106#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:105-106#2/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:4:105-106#2/r7.claim: The Prophet must not defend someone who betrayed a Muslim or a protected non-Muslim in person or property against the party seeking the right that was violated.
TABRISI:4:105-106#2/r7.anchor: نهاه أن يكون لمن خان مسلما أو معاهدا في نفسه أو ماله خصيما

TABRISI:4:105-106#2/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:105-106#2/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:4:105-106#2/r9.claim: Although addressed to the Prophet, the admonition is for his community: he defended someone who appeared just and faithful but was inwardly otherwise; God is exalted above all sins and indecencies.
TABRISI:4:105-106#2/r9.anchor: والخطاب وإن توجه إلى النبي من حيث خاصم عمن رآه على ظاهر الإيمان والعدالة وكان في الباطن بخلافه

TABRISI:4:105-106#2/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:105-106#2/r10.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:4:105-106#2/r10.claim: Another account says the Prophet did not actually defend the accused; he only intended to, and God reproached him for that intention.
TABRISI:4:105-106#2/r10.anchor: وقيل: إنه لم يخاصم عن الخصم وإنما هم بذلك فعاتبه الله عليه

TABRISI:4:105-106#2/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:105-106#2/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:4:105-106#2/r11.claim: The verse follows the discussion of hypocrites and disbelievers with a command to avoid defending traitors; another connection is that, after legal rulings, it affirms that all were sent in truth.
TABRISI:4:105-106#2/r11.anchor: وجه اتصال الآية بما قبلها أنه لما تقدم ذكر المنافقين والكافرين والأمر بمجانبتهم عقب ذلك بذكر الخائنين

TABRISI:4:105-106#2/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:105-106#2/r12.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:4:105-106#2/r12.claim: Another account of the connection is that after explaining the rulings and laws in the sūra, God states that all of them were sent in truth.
TABRISI:4:105-106#2/r12.anchor: وقيل: إنه تعالى لما بين الأحكام والشرائع في السورة عقبها بأن جميع ذلك أنزل بالحق

THALABI:v3p380/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p380/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v3p380/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says Taʿma of Banu Zafar stole Qatada ibn al-Nuʿman's armor in a leaking flour sack and hid it with Zayd ibn al-Samin. His clan urged the Prophet to defend him, and revelation condemned that plea.
THALABI:v3p380/r4.anchor: قال الكلبي عن أبي صالح عن ابن عباس: نزلت هذه الآية في رجل من الأنصار

THALABI:v3p380/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p380/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v3p380/r5.claim: In another version, Taʿma stole an Ansari's armor in a sack of bran; its trail led to Zayd ibn al-Samin, and the Prophet nearly ordered the Jewish man's hand cut off before the verse came down.
THALABI:v3p380/r5.anchor: وفي رواية أخرى عن ابن عباس قال: إن طعمة سرق درعا من أنصاري

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p69#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p69#2/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p69#2/r1.claim: Exegetes agree that this verse and those following concern Ṭuʿma ibn Ubayriq: he stole armor and implicated a Jew; his party asked the Prophet to defend him, and he nearly accepted the case against the Jew.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p69#2/r1.anchor: أجمعوا على أن هذه الآية وما بعدها من أي كثير نزلت في قصة طعمة ابن أبيرق

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p69#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p69#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس، الضحاك، السدي، الحسن، ابن زيد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p69#2/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas, al-Dahhak, al-Suddi, al-Hasan, and Ibn Zayd say Ṭuʿma stole the armor and accused the Jew of stealing it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p69#2/r2.anchor: والضحاك والسدي والحسن وابن زيد أن طعمة سرق الدرع

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p69#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p69#2/r3.speaker: مجاهد ومقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p69#2/r3.claim: Mujahid and Muqatil say Ṭuʿma had been entrusted with the Jew's armor without witnesses, denied receiving it, and accused the Jew of theft.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p70/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p70/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p70/r1.claim: The Book was sent with truth, meaning on the side of truth rather than falsehood; it can also be called true in the sense that it possesses truth.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p70/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p70/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p70/r2.claim: God's description as al-Haqq in 22:62 illustrates the sense of possessing truth.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p70/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p70/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p70/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses what God showed the Prophet as what God taught him.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p70/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p70/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p70/r4.claim: Other exegetes give the same sense, as when 34:6 uses seeing to mean knowing.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p70/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p70/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p70/r5.claim: The verse indicates that the Prophet's judgment was wholly based on revelation.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p70/r5.anchor: وهذا يدل أن رأيه - صلى الله عليه وسلم - كله وحيا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p70/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p70/r6.speaker: عمر
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p70/r6.claim: Umar warned people not to say they judged as God showed them, since God did this only for His Prophet; the Prophet's view was correct by revelation, while others rely on conjecture and effort.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p70/r6.anchor: فإن الله تعالى لم يفعل ذلك إلا لنبيه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p70/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p70/r7.speaker: الحسن
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p70/r7.claim: Al-Hasan says prophets' judgments are revelation and cites this verse.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p70/r7.anchor: وقال الحسن: "رأي الأنبياء عليهم السلام وحي"

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p70/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p70/r8.speaker: أبو علي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p70/r8.claim: Abu Ali rules out eyesight because adjudicating disputes is not perceived by sight, and rules out a form taking two objects, which causative transfer would make take three; the construction instead derives from raʾā meaning to hold an opinion, which takes one object and two after transfer.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p70/r8.anchor: قال أبو علي: لا يخلو (أراك) من أن يكون

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p72/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p72/r1.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p72/r1.claim: Al-Zajjaj explains the warning as forbidding the Prophet from litigating for or defending a traitor.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p72/r1.anchor: قال الزجاج: أي لا تكن مخاصما ولا دافعا عن خائن

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p72/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p72/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p72/r2.claim: Khaṣīm is a disputant, plural khuṣamāʾ; the root refers to an edge or side, whence litigants take opposite sides and a cloud has sides called khuṣūm.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p72/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p72/r3.speaker: الأخطل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p72/r3.claim: Al-Akhtal's line illustrates khuṣūm as the sides of a cloud that answer each other with thunder; the south wind drives it along.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p72/r3.anchor: قال الأخطل (¬4): إذا طعنت فيها الجنوب تحاملت ... باعجاز جرار تداعى خصومها

QASHANI:4:105-108/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:4:105-108/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:4:105-108/r1.claim: The revealed Book is detailed knowledge of the attributes and their manifestations and rulings, grounded in truth and justice, enabling judgment among people.
QASHANI:4:105-108/r1.anchor: أي: علم تفاصيل الصفات وأحكام تجلياتها بالحق ملتبسا بالعدل والصدق

QASHANI:4:105-108/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:4:105-108/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:4:105-108/r2.claim: The Prophet judges by the divine justice God shows him, not by his own self.
QASHANI:4:105-108/r2.anchor: أو قائما بالحق لا بنفسك لتكون حاكما بين الخلق

QASHANI:4:105-108/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:4:105-108/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:4:105-108/r3.claim: The traitors fail the primordial trust of knowing God deposited in their capacities, betraying themselves and others by misusing rights.
QASHANI:4:105-108/r3.anchor: الذين لا يؤدون أمانة الله التي أودعها عندهم في الأزل بما ركز في استعدادهم من إمكان كمال معرفته

QASHANI:4:105-108/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:4:105-108/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:4:105-108/r4.claim: The Prophet must not defend traitors from punishment or others' retaliation, or plead that God wronged them; they are wrongdoers with no defense.
QASHANI:4:105-108/r4.anchor: يدفع عنهم العذاب وتسليط الله الخلق عليهم بالإيذاء ويحتج عنهم على غيرهم

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:105-106/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:105-106/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:105-106/r1.claim: The verses concern Tuʿma ibn Ubayriq, who stole a coat of mail, planted it with a Jew, and accused him; the two groups brought the dispute to the Prophet, and Tuʿma's people asked him to defend their man. The Prophet considered it before revelation.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:105-106/r1.anchor: هذه الآية وما بعدها نزلت في قصة طعمة بن أبيرق؛ سرق درعا، ثم رمى بها يهوديا، فلما طلبت منه الدرع أحال على اليهودي، ورماه بالسرقة،

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:105-106/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:105-106/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:105-106/r2.claim: God sent scripture in truth for judgment, not for unjust transgression.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:105-106/r2.anchor: { إنا أنزلنا إليك الكتاب بالحق } في الحكم لا بالتعدي فيه

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:105-106/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:105-106/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:105-106/r3.claim: Judging by what God showed means judging by what He taught.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:105-106/r3.anchor: { لتحكم بين الناس بما أراك الله } أي: فيما علمك الله

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:105-106/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:105-106/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:105-106/r4.claim: The traitors are Tuʿma and his people; the Prophet is told not to argue for them.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:105-106/r4.anchor: { ولا تكن للخائنين } طعمة وقومه { خصيما } مخاصما عنهم

ELMALILI:4:105-106/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:105-106/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:105-106/r1.claim: The Qur'an is a fully reliable guide revealed in truth, setting out people's rights before God and one another and showing justice, truth, and sincerity without falsehood or deviation.
ELMALILI:4:105-106/r1.anchor: bu kitâb-ı ekmeli, bu Kur’ân-ı azîmü’ş-şân’ı hak ile, Hak teâlâ’nın insanlar üzerinde insanların ferden veya cem‘an yekdiğeri beynindeki hukūkun künhünü muhtevî

ELMALILI:4:105-106/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:105-106/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:105-106/r2.claim: The Prophet is to settle every doctrinal or practical dispute by God's truth and absolute revelation, giving everyone equally the right they deserve.
ELMALILI:4:105-106/r2.anchor: Allah’ın sana gösterdiği ilm-i hak ve vahy-i mutlak ile hükmedesin.

ELMALILI:4:105-106/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:105-106/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:105-106/r3.claim: The book's central purpose is to establish a basis for judging; the Prophet's distinctive task is to use revelation and its knowledge as the sole standard where revelation has spoken.
ELMALILI:4:105-106/r3.anchor: Peygamber’in min tarafillah vârid olan vahyi ve vahiyden mütehassıl ilmi müstakillen medâr-ı hükm ittihaz etmesi

ELMALILI:4:105-106/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:105-106/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:105-106/r4.claim: Other proofs are only outward appearances, whereas revelation is necessary knowledge corresponding to the truth's essence.
ELMALILI:4:105-106/r4.anchor: delâil-i sâire sırf zâhirî olduğu hâlde vahiy künh-i hakka muntabık bir ilm-i zarûrîdir.

ELMALILI:4:105-106/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:105-106/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:105-106/r5.claim: A judge must pursue truth rather than personal preference and must never decide against a right he knows with certainty; the verse validates knowledge only when it is witnessed certainty, not opinion or ijtihād.
ELMALILI:4:105-106/r5.anchor: Burada ilm-i hâkimin muteber olduğuna bir delil vardır. Fakat bunun bir re’y ü ictihad değil, bir ilm-i şuhûdî olması şarttır.

ELMALILI:4:105-106/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:105-106/r6.speaker: Hazret-i Ömer
ELMALILI:4:105-106/r6.claim: Umar warns people not to call their own opinion something God showed them: that wording denotes revelation particular to the Prophet, while their opinions remain conjecture.

ELMALILI:4:105-106/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:105-106/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:105-106/r7.claim: Judges cannot rule from mere opinion or conviction; they must investigate evidentiary means and follow what those proofs establish.
ELMALILI:4:105-106/r7.anchor: hâkimler mücerred re’y ü kanaatleriyle hükmedemezler. Esbâb ve vesâit-i sübûtiye taharrîsine ve onların delâletine ittibâ‘a mecburdurlar.

ELMALILI:4:105-106/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:105-106/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:105-106/r8.claim: Because the goal is to reach the truth, a judge may never rule against a fact known through witnessed certainty.
ELMALILI:4:105-106/r8.anchor: maksad-ı aslî hakka isabet olduğundan hâkimin ilm-i şühûdî ile mâlumu olan bir hususta ilmi hilâfına hükmetmesi asla câiz olmaz.

ELMALILI:4:105-106/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:105-106/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:105-106/r9.claim: Do not defend traitors or feud against innocent people on their behalf, even if the innocent belong to another community; do not act as their lawyer.
ELMALILI:4:105-106/r9.anchor: kim olursa olsun, velevse ümmetinden bulunsun hâinleri müdafaa için berî olanlara velevse millet-i âhardan olsun husumet etme.

ELMALILI:4:105-106/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:105-106/r10.speaker: المفسرون
ELMALILI:4:105-106/r10.claim: Commentators agree that the passage was revealed about the Banū Ubayriq affair; Kirmānī specifies Tuʿma ibn Ubayriq of Banū Ẓafar ibn al-Ḥārith.
ELMALILI:4:105-106/r10.anchor: Bu âyetlerin Benî Übeyrık vak‘ası hakkında nâzil olduğunda müfessirînin ittifâkı nakl olunuyor. Ebû Hayyân’ın nakline göre Kirmânî demiştir

ELMALILI:4:105-106/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:105-106/r11.speaker: İbn Bahr
ELMALILI:4:105-106/r11.claim: Ibn Bahr says the verses concern hypocrites and are connected to 4:88; Elmalılı says this need not conflict with the consensus because Tuʿma, called Bashīr, was a hypocrite.
ELMALILI:4:105-106/r11.anchor: İbn Bahr demiştir ki münafıklar hakkında nâzil oldu

ELMALILI:4:105-106/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:105-106/r12.speaker: Râzî
ELMALILI:4:105-106/r12.claim: Rāzī says commentators agree that most of these verses were revealed about Tuʿma ibn Ubayriq, though reports differ over the incident's details.
ELMALILI:4:105-106/r12.anchor: Bunun için Râzî ıtlâkı üzere der ki: Bu âyetlerin ekserîsi Tu‘me b. Übeyrık hakkında nâzil olduğunda müfessirîn müttefiktir.

ELMALILI:4:105-106/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:105-106/r13.speaker: Râzî
ELMALILI:4:105-106/r13.claim: One reported version says Tuʿma stole armor and, when pursued, blamed a Jew.
ELMALILI:4:105-106/r13.anchor: Birisi Tu‘me zırhlı bir gömlek sirkat etmiş, talep olununca sirkati bir Yahudîye atfetmiş.

ELMALILI:4:105-106/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:105-106/r14.speaker: Râzî
ELMALILI:4:105-106/r14.claim: A second version says the armor had been entrusted to Tuʿma, who denied taking it when asked; a third says he accused the Jew when questioned.
ELMALILI:4:105-106/r14.anchor: İkincisi: Zırh kendisine vedî‘a bırakılmış, şâhid de yokmuş, talep olununca inkâr etmiş. Üçüncüsü: Talep edildiği zaman Yahudînin çaldığını iddia etmiş.

ELMALILI:4:105-106/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:105-106/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:105-106/r15.claim: Elmalılı prefers the majority's account: Tuʿma stole armor from neighbor Qatāda ibn Nuʿmān, hid it in a flour sack, and its trail led to Jew Zayd ibn Samīn, who said Tuʿma had left it with him.
ELMALILI:4:105-106/r15.anchor: Ekser müfessirînin muhtârına göre rivayetlerin hâsılı şudur: Ensar meyânında Benî Zafer’den Tu‘me b. Übeyrık nâmında birisi komşusu Katâde b. Numan’dan bir gece bir un dağarcığı içinde bir dir‘-zırh- çalmış

ELMALILI:4:105-106/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:105-106/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:105-106/r16.claim: In that account, Banū Ẓafar vouched for Tuʿma, asked the Prophet to acquit him and blame the Jew, and urged defense of Tuʿma; revelation identified the guilty and innocent party.
ELMALILI:4:105-106/r16.anchor: Tu‘me’yi müdafaa edip Müslümanlık nâmına Yahudîlerle mücadele eylemesini rica eylemişler.

ELMALILI:4:105-106/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:105-106/r17.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:105-106/r17.claim: According to the preferred account, the Prophet initially leaned toward defending Tuʿma on the basis of his oath and the tribe's testimony, but revelation exposed the traitor and innocent party.
ELMALILI:4:105-106/r17.anchor: Resûlullah da zâhirde Müslüman olan Tu‘me’nin yeminine ve bunların şehadetine binâen öyle yapmak istemiş, bunun üzerine min tarafillah bu âyetler nâzil olmuş

ELMALILI:4:105-106/r18.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:105-106/r18.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:105-106/r18.claim: Rather than repent, Tuʿma fled to Mecca and apostatized; after further thefts and expulsion, accounts say he died under a collapsing wall or was killed after robbing a merchant caravan, and 4:115 then came down regarding apostates' fate.
ELMALILI:4:105-106/r18.anchor: Tu‘me hakka teslim olup tevbekâr olacak yerde Mekke’ye kaçmış ve irtidad etmiş.

ELMALILI:4:105-106/r19.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:105-106/r19.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:105-106/r19.claim: In the occasion of revelation, the traitors are Tuʿma and his helpers; generally the wording applies to unjust and immoral people like them.
ELMALILI:4:105-106/r19.anchor: sebeb-i nüzûle nazaran “hâinîn”den murad bu Tu‘me ve buna mu‘âvenet edenler, sûret-i umûmiyede de bu gibi haksızlar ve ahlâksızlardır.

ELMALILI:4:105-106#2/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:105-106#2/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:105-106#2/r1.claim: The responsibility of judges, witnesses, and advocates is grave; even an unwitting inclination toward a traitor against an innocent person, misled by outward evidence, is itself a fault.
ELMALILI:4:105-106#2/r1.anchor: hâkimin velev bilmeyerek olsun velevse esbâb-ı zâhireye aldanarak olsun bir hâin lehine meyledip berî’ü’z-zimme olan bir kimseye husumet etmesi haddizâtında bir kusur olduğunu

ELMALILI:4:105-106#2/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:105-106#2/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:105-106#2/r2.claim: God protected the Prophet from this fault and granted knowledge of the unseen, after his inclination to defend Tuʿma based on outward Islam and his tribe's request and testimony.
ELMALILI:4:105-106#2/r2.anchor: İslâm-ı zâhirîye ve kavminin talep ve şehadetine binâen Tu‘me’yi müdafaaya meyletmiş olmasından dolayı Peygamber’i hatâdan sıyânet ederken

ELMALILI:4:105-106#2/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:105-106#2/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:105-106#2/r5.claim: The warning severely condemns knowingly aiding treachery and injustice, promoting wrong for gain, prejudice, or collusion, and judges who follow desire instead of right; it also urges repentance.
ELMALILI:4:105-106#2/r5.anchor: haksızların haksızlıklarını bile bile zulm ü hıyanete mu‘âvenet edenlere ve

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:105/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:105/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:105/r1.claim: The ten-verse passage explains how the Prophet and, through him, the Muslim community should act in disputes; specific occasions introduce general rules for Muslims through the end of time.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:105/r1.anchor: Bu on âyette insanların arasında meydana gelen anlaşmazlıklar, davalar, tartışmalar karşısında Hz. Peygamber’in ve daha ziyade onun şahsında ümmetinin takınması gereken tavır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:105/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:105/r2.speaker: Tirmizî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:105/r2.claim: Tirmidhi reports that Rifaa b. Zayd’s flour and weapons were stolen by an Ubeyriq family member, who blamed innocent Lebid; after the family complained to Muhammad, he reproached Katada for accusing Muslims without proof, and the verses were revealed.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:105/r2.anchor: Bu olay üzerine yukarıda meâli verilen âyetler nâzil oldu (Tirmizî, “Tefsîr”, 5/22).

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:105/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:105/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:105/r3.claim: The clause about judging by what God shows explains why He sent down the Book containing truth: it gives facts, norms, methods, general and specific rulings, and knowledge.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:105/r3.anchor: “Allah’ın sana gösterdiğine göre hükmedesin diye...” ifadesi “hakkı içeren kitabı indirme”nin gerekçesini açıklamaktadır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:105/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:105/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:105/r4.claim: God teaches truth first through Qur’anic revelation; secondarily, the Sunnah is a source because God communicates its meanings and rulings and keeps the Prophet’s actions, including ijtihad, under divine oversight.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:105/r4.anchor: İkinci derecede gerçeğin kaynağı sünnettir. Sünnet hem mâna ve hükmün Allah tarafından bildirilmesi hem de Hz. Peygamber’in, içinde ictihada dayalı olanların da bulunduğu bütün tasarruflarının ilâhî kontrol altında bulunması bakımından bu özelliği taşımaktadır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:105/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:105/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:105/r5.claim: The Prophet cannot err in understanding the Qur’an or applying its universal principles to particular matters, since these tasks belong to conveying the message; other people can err in ijtihad.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:105/r5.anchor: Hz. Peygamber’in Kur’an’ı anlama, küllî kuralları özel konulara, ilişkilere ve problemlere uygulama hususunda hata etmesi mümkün değildir. Çünkü bunlar peygamberlerin aslî vazifeleri olan tebliğe dahildir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:105/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:105/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:105/r6.claim: In deciding the facts of an individual case, even the Prophet must rely on objective evidence and means of proof, like other judges, and may err in the verdict.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:105/r6.anchor: Kanunu belli bir olaya ve davaya uygulama, yani yargılama ve hüküm verme alanına gelince burada Hz. Peygamber de objektif verilere, ispat vasıtalarına dayanmak mecburiyetindedir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:105/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:105/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:105/r7.claim: Applied to the theft, Qur’anic rules forbid siding with an apparent wrongdoer, shifting guilt to another, or slandering; people remain dependent on God’s guidance for knowledge and judgment.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:105/r7.anchor: mahkemeye getirilen davalarda hain ve haksız olduğu anlaşılan tarafı tutmamak ve savunmamak gerektiğini bildiriyor; bir suç veya günah işleyenin bunu başkasına atmasını, iftira ve bühtanda bulunmasını yasaklıyor

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:105/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:105/r8.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:105/r8.claim: A judge misled by false witnesses or a strong but unjust defense might rule against innocent Lebid rather than the thief’s son; if the judge follows proper procedure, responsibility rests on the deceivers and he is even rewarded.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:105/r8.anchor: Meselâ yalancı şahitlere dayanarak veya haksızın güçlü savunmasının etkisi altında kalarak hatalı bir hüküm verebilir, Übeyrık’ın oğlu yerine kendisine iftira atılan Lebîd veya onun gibi bir suçsuz aleyhine hükmedebilir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:105/r9.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:105/r9.speaker: Hz. Peygamber
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:105/r9.claim: The Prophet says he is human and may decide for a party whose argument is more persuasive; a person awarded another’s right must not take it, since it is a piece of fire.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:105/r9.anchor: bizzat Hz. Peygamber şöyle açıklamıştır: “Ben ancak bir beşerim ve siz bana davalarla geliyorsunuz.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:105/r10.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:105/r10.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:105/r10.claim: Some use this verse to deny that the Prophet could rule through ijtihad, but the author rejects that reading because sound evidence establishes his ijtihad, occasional error, and divine correction.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:105/r10.anchor: Bu âyeti, Hz. Peygamber’in ictihadla hükmetmesinin câiz olmadığına delil gösterenler olmuşsa da bu delillendirme tutarlı değildir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:105/r11.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:105/r11.speaker: Râzî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:105/r11.claim: Razi explains that judging by what God shows includes applying and extending general or particular revealed texts through interpretation; analogical reasoning is still text-based because it takes a text as its measure.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:105/r11.anchor: Râzî’nin deyişiyle “Esasen kıyas ederek hükmetmek de nasla hükmetmek demektir. Çünkü kıyas yapan nastan hareket etmekte, onu ölçü olarak almaktadır”

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:105/r12.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:105/r12.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:105/r12.claim: The ban on defending traitors is reinforced by 4:109 and particularly addresses judges and lawyers, whose task is to establish rights and bring them to their owners.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:105/r12.anchor: “Hainlerden taraf olmak, onları savunmak” yasaklanıyor, 109. âyette de “Kıyamet günü Allah’a karşı onları kim savunacak yahut onlara kim vekil olacak?” diye soruluyor.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:105/r13.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:105/r13.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:105/r13.claim: Judges and lawyers must not favor an unjust client because of rank, wealth, fame, or benefit, and should use their skills to reveal the truth rather than secure an undeserved win.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:105/r13.anchor: Davacının mevkii, şöhreti, serveti, rütbesi, sağladığı menfaat ne olursa olsun hâkim ve vekiller haksız olduğu halde onun tarafını tutmayacak

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:105/r14.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:105/r14.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:105/r14.claim: Advocacy retains legitimacy when lawyers defend rightful claims, seek settlement in unjust cases, and help ensure fairness in penalties and compensation.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:105/r14.anchor: Avukatların bu anlayış ve ahlâk içinde hareket etmeleri yani haklıların davalarını savunmaları ve haksızların davalarında sulhu aramak, cezada ve tazminatta adalet ve hakkaniyetin gerçekleşmesine katkıda bulunmak

BURHAN:v4p340/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p340/r3.speaker: الراغب
BURHAN:v4p340/r3.claim: Al-Rāghib reads the lām as ‘on behalf of/because of the traitors’: do not litigate for them. He equates it with ‘do not argue for those who betray themselves,’ unlike ‘be an adversary of God.’
BURHAN:v4p340/r3.anchor: وليست كالتي في قولك لا تكن لله خصيما

SULAMI:v1p159#2/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p159#2/r1.speaker: سهل
SULAMI:v1p159#2/r1.claim: Sahl says the judgment is by the wisdom God taught the Prophet in the Quran and religious law.
SULAMI:v1p159#2/r1.anchor: قال سهل : بما علمك الله من الحكمة في القرآن والشريعة

SULAMI:v1p159#2/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p159#2/r2.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p159#2/r2.claim: Another reading says to judge by what God unveils directly, not merely by what people show outwardly, since the Prophet's vision is unveiling and direct witnessing.
SULAMI:v1p159#2/r2.anchor: وقال بعضهم : لتحكم بين الناس بما أراك وأظهره لك

SULAMI:v1p159#2/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p159#2/r3.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v1p159#2/r3.claim: Ibn Ata says the Prophet sees through God, speaks from God, and remains always within God's sight and hearing.
SULAMI:v1p159#2/r3.anchor: وقال ابن عطاء في هذه الآية : بما أراك الله فإنك بنا ترى وعنا تنطق

ITQAN:v4p467/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p467/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p467/r1.claim: To interpret the Qurʾan, first explain its general or condensed passages from other Qurʾanic passages where they are expanded; Ibn al-Jawzi wrote a book on such cross-explanations.
ITQAN:v4p467/r1.anchor: طلبه أولا من القرآن فما أجمل منه في مكان فقد فسر في موضع آخر

ITQAN:v4p467/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p467/r2.speaker: الشافعي
ITQAN:v4p467/r2.claim: If the Qurʾan does not settle the point, consult the Sunna, which explains it; al-Shafiʿi says every ruling the Messenger made came from what God showed him in the Qurʾan.
ITQAN:v4p467/r2.anchor: فإن أعياه ذلك طلبه من السنة فإنها شارحة للقرآن وموضحة له وقد قال الشافعي

ITQAN:v4p467/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p467/r3.speaker: الحاكم
ITQAN:v4p467/r3.claim: When the Qurʾan and Sunna do not settle the interpretation, consult the Companions, who witnessed the circumstances of revelation; al-Hakim says a Companion’s tafsir from an eyewitness has the status of a Prophetic report.
ITQAN:v4p467/r3.anchor: فإن لم يجده في السنة رجع إلى أقوال الصحابة فإنهم أدرى بذلك لما شاهدوه من القرائن

ITQAN:v4p467/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p467/r4.speaker: أبو طالب الطبري
ITQAN:v4p467/r4.claim: Abu Talib al-Tabari requires a sound creed and adherence to the Sunna, warning that religiously suspect or partisan interpreters may mislead people away from the Salaf and the path of guidance.
ITQAN:v4p467/r4.anchor: اعلم أن من شرطه صحة الاعتقاد أولا ولزوم سنة الدين فإن من كان مغموصا عليه في دينه

ITQAN:v4p467/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p467/r5.speaker: أبو طالب الطبري
ITQAN:v4p467/r5.claim: The interpreter should rely on transmitted material from the Prophet, Companions, and their contemporaries and avoid innovations; reconcile differing Companion explanations when possible, since they may express one underlying meaning.
ITQAN:v4p467/r5.anchor: ويجب أن يكون اعتماده على النقل عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وعن أصحابه ومن عاصرهم

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p321/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p321/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p321/r1.claim: The poem calls wealth’s increase life and its spending death, then metaphorically assigns life to weapons and killing to smiles and generosity.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p321/r1.anchor: جعل الزيادة والوفور حياة في المال وتفريقه في العطاء قتلا ثم أثبت الحياة فعلا للصوارم والقتل فعلا للتبسم

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p321/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p321/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p321/r2.claim: Saying dinars and dirhams destroy people treats the temptation they cause as destruction, attributing an act to coins that cannot act.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p321/r2.anchor: أهلك الناس الدينار والدرهم جعل الفتنة هلاكا على المجاز ثم أثبت الهلاك فعلا للدينار والدرهم وليسا مما يفعلان

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p321/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p321/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p321/r3.claim: Metaphor in the attribution of an action is judged by reason; metaphor in the predicate itself is a linguistic transfer.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p321/r3.anchor: إذا وقع في الإثبات فهو متلقي من العقل فإذا عرض في المثبت فهو متلقي من اللغة

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p321/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p321/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p321/r4.claim: Reason assesses whether an action or quality is truly assigned to someone; language itself neither affirms nor denies such judgments.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p321/r4.anchor: علمت أن مأخذه العقل وأنه القاضي فيه دون اللغة لأن اللغة لم تأت لتحكم بحكم

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p321/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p321/r5.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p321/r5.claim: When the transferred word is the predicate, as in giving life to earth through rain, metaphor is grounded in language and likeness.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p321/r5.anchor: فإنما كان مأخذه اللغة لأجل أن طريقه المجاز بأن أجرى اسم الحياة

TUSTARI:4:105/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:4:105/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:4:105/r1.claim: God showed the Prophet the wisdom of the Quran and the laws of Islam by which to judge among people.
TUSTARI:4:105/r1.anchor: يعني بما علمك الله تعالى من الحكمة في القرآن وشرائع الإسلام

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p82/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p82/r1.speaker: قتادة بن النعمان
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p82/r1.claim: Qatada ibn al-Numan reports that Banu Ubayriq stole his uncle’s food and weapons, blamed Labid, and accused Qatada and his uncle; revelation vindicated them and exposed the thieves. Al-Hakim graded the report sound on Muslim’s criteria.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p82/r1.anchor: عن قتادة ابن النعمان قال كان أهل بيت منا يقال لهم بنو أبيرق بشر وبشير ومبشر

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p83/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p83/r1.speaker: محمود بن لبيد
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p83/r1.claim: Mahmud ibn Labid says Bashir stole food and two suits of armor from Rifa'a’s loft, denied it, and blamed Labid; revelation exposed Bashir and cleared Labid.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p83/r1.anchor: عن محمود بن لبيد قال عدا بشير ابن الحرث على علية رفاعة بن زيد عم قتادة بن النعمان

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p180/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p180/r3.speaker: جماعة من المفسرين
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p180/r3.claim: A group of exegetes says the passage through 4:116 was revealed in one case: Ta'ma ibn Ubayriq stole Qatada ibn al-Nu'man's armor, hid it with a Jew, and his tribe asked Muhammad to defend him; revelation came as he inclined to support them.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p180/r3.anchor: فهم رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم أن يفعل، وكان هواه معهم وأن يعاقب اليهودي، حتى أنزل الله تعالى: {إنا أنزلنا إليك الكتاب بالحق} الآية كلها، وهذا قول جماعة من المفسرين.

DAMGHANI:v1p186/r6.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p186/r6.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p186/r6.claim: Raʾā can mean to know or teach; the Prophet judges by what God has made known to him.
DAMGHANI:v1p186/r6.anchor: يرى يعلم قوله تعالى في سورة سبأ

DAMGHANI:v1p166/r1.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p166/r1.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p166/r1.claim: Khiyāna can mean betraying a trust; the source applies it to the person who stole a coat of mail.
DAMGHANI:v1p166/r1.anchor: الخيانة التي تكون ضد الأمانة فيخون بها قوله تعالى في سورة النساء

DAMGHANI:v1p166/r2.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p166/r2.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p166/r2.claim: Dāmghānī says the verse was revealed about Tuʿma ibn Ubayriq, who had stolen an iron coat of mail in his possession.
DAMGHANI:v1p166/r2.anchor: نزلت في طعمة بن أبيرق خان في درع من حديد كانت عنده

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p319/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p319/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p319/r1.claim: Ruʾya originally means perceiving an object with the eye; rawāʾ means good appearance.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p319/r1.anchor: الرؤية في الأصل : إدراك المرئي بالعين . والرواء : حسن المنظر

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p319/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p319/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p319/r2.claim: The unhamzated ruʾya is connected to raʾawtu when considering or deliberating an issue.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p319/r2.anchor: والروية غير مهموزة : وأصلها من روأت في الأمر إذا دبرته

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p319/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p319/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p319/r3.claim: Rawī is the fixed letter of a poem's rhyme.

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p319/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p319/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p319/r4.claim: The related forms distinguish seeing, opinion, drinking one's fill, transmitting a report, and ostentation in action.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p319/r4.anchor: وتقول : رأيت الشيء رؤية . ورأيت من الفكر رأيا . ورويت من الماء ريا

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p319/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p319/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p319/r5.claim: Ruʾya means seeing and visual inspection in 39:60, 63:4, and 76:20.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p319/r5.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن الرؤية في القرآن على ستة أوجه : - أحدها : النظر والمعاينة

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p319/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p319/r6.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p319/r6.claim: Here ruʾya means knowledge or instruction; the source groups 2:128, 21:30, 34:6, and 71:15 with this sense.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p319/r6.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن الرؤية في القرآن على ستة أوجه

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p319/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p319/r7.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p319/r7.claim: Ruʾya means reflection or consideration in 16:79.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p319/r7.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن الرؤية في القرآن على ستة أوجه

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p319/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p319/r8.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p319/r8.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن الرؤية في القرآن على ستة أوجه

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p319/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p319/r9.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p319/r9.claim: The expression can convey wonder in 4:49 and 4:60.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p319/r9.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن الرؤية في القرآن على ستة أوجه

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p319/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p319/r10.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p319/r10.claim: The expression can mean informing or telling in 2:258 and 105:1.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p319/r10.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن الرؤية في القرآن على ستة أوجه

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p281/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p281/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p281/r1.claim: Khiyana is failing in what one is entrusted with, opposite of trustworthiness; takhawwan also means to diminish or shortchange.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p281/r1.anchor: الخيانة : التفريط فيما يؤتمن الإنسان عليه . ونقيضها : الأمانة . والتخون في اللغة : التنقص

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p281/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p281/r2.speaker: ثعلب
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p281/r2.claim: Thaʿlab says it is plausible that the bowl called khuwan takes its name from diminishing what is owed.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p281/r2.anchor: وسئل ثعلب : أيجوز أن يقال : إن الخوان إنما سمي بذلك لأنه يتخون ما عليه ، أي : ينتقص ، فقال : ما يبعد ذلك

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p281/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p281/r3.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p281/r3.claim: Khiyana means disobedience in 2:187, 8:27, and 40:19; Ibn Qutayba glosses 2:187 as disobeying oneself.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p281/r3.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن الخيانة [ في القرآن ] على خمسة أوجه : - أحدها : المعصية

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p281/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p281/r4.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p281/r4.claim: Khiyana means breaking a pact in 5:13 and 8:58.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p281/r4.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن الخيانة [ في القرآن ] على خمسة أوجه

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p281/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p281/r5.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p281/r5.claim: Khiyana means failing to keep a trust; this verse concerns Tuʿma ibn Abayriq and his stolen armor.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p281/r5.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن الخيانة [ في القرآن ] على خمسة أوجه

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p281/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p281/r6.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p281/r6.claim: The source says 4:105 was revealed about Tuʿma ibn Abayriq, who hid the stolen armor with a Jewish man.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p281/r6.anchor: نزلت في طعمة بن أبيرق ، كان عنده درع فخانها

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p281/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p281/r7.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p281/r7.claim: Khiyana means disloyalty in religion in 4:107, 8:71, and 66:10.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p281/r7.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن الخيانة [ في القرآن ] على خمسة أوجه

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p281/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p281/r8.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p281/r8.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن الخيانة [ في القرآن ] على خمسة أوجه

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p271/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p271/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p271/r2.claim: Ruʾya can mean knowledge: God taught the Prophet how to judge, and other verses use seeing for knowing or being taught.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p271/r2.anchor: والرؤية: علم، كقوله: أولم ير الذين كفروا أن السماوات والأرض كانتا رتقا

NAHHAS:v1p485/r15.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p485/r15.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p485/r15.anchor: لام كي وروي عن الحسن وأبي عمرو أنهما أدغما الميم

NAHHAS:v1p485/r16.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p485/r16.speaker: الحسن وأبو عمرو
NAHHAS:v1p485/r16.claim: Al-Hasan and Abu Amr are reported to assimilate mīm into bāʾ, though grammarians disallow it because mīm is nasalized.
NAHHAS:v1p485/r16.anchor: وروي عن الحسن وأبي عمرو أنهما أدغما الميم في الباء ولا يجيز ذلك النحويون

SAMIN-DURR:4:105/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:105/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:4:105/r1.claim: Bi-l-ḥaqq is an emphatic circumstantial phrase modifying the Book: God sent it down clothed in truth.
SAMIN-DURR:4:105/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى: { بالحق }: في محل نصب على الحال المؤكدة فيتعلق بمحذوف، وصاحب الحال هو الكتاب

SAMIN-DURR:4:105/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:105/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:4:105/r3.claim: Arāka takes two objects, a deleted relative pronoun and the second-person suffix; raʾā may mean opinion or knowledge, and takes one object before causativization and two after.
SAMIN-DURR:4:105/r3.anchor: و " أراك " متعد لاثنين أحدهما العائد المحذوف، والثاني كاف الخطاب

SAMIN-DURR:4:105/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:105/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:4:105/r4.claim: Li-l-khāʾinīn attaches to khaṣīman with the ordinary purposive lām; reading it as ʿan is unnecessary because the sense works without that change.
SAMIN-DURR:4:105/r4.anchor: و " للخائنين " متعلق ب " خصيما " واللام للتعليل على بابها

SAMIN-DURR:4:105/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:105/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:4:105/r5.claim: Khaṣīman has an omitted object, estimated as al-barīʾ; it may be an intensive pattern like ḍarīb or a reciprocal form like khalīṭ and jalīs, meaning disputant.
SAMIN-DURR:4:105/r5.anchor: وخصيم يجوز أن يكون مثال مبالغة كضريب

ZAJJAJ:v2p99/r13.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p99/r13.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p99/r13.claim: God showed the Prophet the truth by revealing it to him.
ZAJJAJ:v2p99/r13.anchor: أي بالحق الذي أعلمكه الله عز وجل.

ZAJJAJ:v2p101/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p101/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p101/r1.claim: Do not litigate or defend the cause of a traitor.
ZAJJAJ:v2p101/r1.anchor: أي لا تكن مخاصما ولا دافعا عن خائن.

ZAJJAJ:v2p101/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p101/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p101/r2.claim: An Anṣārī called Abū Ṭuʿma stole armor, hid it in flour, and blamed a Jew; his tribe asked the Prophet to defend him despite knowing the Jew innocent. Revelation exposed him and ordered repentance and judgment by scripture.
ZAJJAJ:v2p101/r2.anchor: ويروى أن رجلا من الأنصار كان يقال له أبو طعمة أو طعمة سرق درعا وجعله في غرارة دقيق،

ZAJJAJ:v2p101/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p101/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p101/r4.claim: A report says Abū Ṭuʿma fled to Mecca, apostatized, and died when a wall collapsed on him as he broke into a house to steal.
ZAJJAJ:v2p101/r4.anchor: ويروى أن أبا طعمة هذا هرب إلى مكة وارتد عن الإسلام، وأنه نقب حائطا بمكة ليسرق أهله فسقط الحائط عليه فقتله.

ASAD-NOTES:4:105#n133/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:4:105#n133/r1.speaker: Asad
ASAD-NOTES:4:105#n133/r1.claim: Though the address directly names the Prophet, Asad says it also applies to everyone who accepts Qur'anic guidance, as the plural address in 4:109 shows.
ASAD-NOTES:4:105#n133/r1.anchor: by implication, however, it is addressed to everyone who has accepted the guidance of the Qur'an

ASAD-NOTES:4:105#n133/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:4:105#n133/r2.speaker: Asad
ASAD-NOTES:4:105#n133/r2.claim: Asad rejects most commentators' exclusively historical explanation as unconvincing because it needlessly limits a self-explanatory ethical teaching of general scope.
ASAD-NOTES:4:105#n133/r2.anchor: the attempt on the part of most of the commentators to explain this passage in purely historical terms is not very convincing

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p55/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p55/r1.speaker: قتادة وغيره
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p55/r1.claim: The main occasion report says the verses concerned Ṭuʿma ibn Ubayriq, who stole Qatāda ibn al-Nuʿmān's armor hidden in a flour sack, denied knowing it, and was exposed when the flour trail led to a Jew who said Ṭuʿma had given it to him.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p55/r1.anchor: نزلت في طعمة بن أبيرق، سرق درعا في جرب فيه دقيق لقتادة بن النعمان وخبأها عند يهودي،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p55/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p55/r2.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p55/r2.claim: An alternate account says Ṭuʿma had entrusted armor to a Jew and betrayed him, then threw it into Abū Malik al-Anṣārī's house when he feared discovery.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p55/r2.anchor: وقيل: استودع يهودي درعا فخانه، فلما خاف اطلاعهم عليها ألقاها في دار أبي مليك الأنصاري.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p55/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p55/r3.speaker: السدي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p55/r3.claim: Al-Suddī's account says the Banū Ubayriq broke into the storage room of Rifāʿa ibn Zayd, Qatāda's uncle, and stole weapons and food; they blamed Labīd ibn Sahl, prompting Qatāda to complain to the Prophet, who considered defending Ṭuʿma or the family.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p55/r3.anchor: قال السدي: وقيل: السلاح والطعام كان لرفاعة بن زيد عم قتادة، وأن بني أبيرق نقبوا مشربيته

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p55/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p55/r4.speaker: الكرماني
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p55/r4.claim: Al-Kirmānī says commentators agree the verses were revealed about Ṭuʿma ibn Ubayriq, except Ibn Baḥr, who says they concern hypocrites and connect to the earlier division over them.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p55/r4.anchor: وقال الكرماني: أجمع المفسرون على أن هذه الآيات نزلت في طعمة بن أبيرق

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p55/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p55/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p55/r5.claim: The verse honors the Messenger and entrusts judgment to him under God's direction.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p55/r5.anchor: وفي هذه الآية تشريف للرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم، وتفويض الأمور إليه بقوله: لتحكم بين الناس

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p55/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p55/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p55/r6.claim: After discussion of hypocrites and rules of fighting, the passage returns to hypocrites who betrayed the Messenger; God exposed their deed and ordered him not to heed them.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p55/r6.anchor: ومناسبة هذه الآية لما قبلها: أنه لما صرح بأحوال المنافقين، واتصل بذلك أمر المحاربة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p55/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p55/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p55/r7.claim: The account identifies Bashīr as a hypocrite who insulted the Companions and falsely attributed poetry to others, while Ṭuʿma apostatized.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p55/r7.anchor: وكان بشير منافقا ويهجو الصحابة وينحل الشعر لغيره، وأما طعمة فارتد،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p55/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p55/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p55/r8.claim: Because the rulings are from God, the Messenger cannot depart from any of them to please a group; even an unbeliever must receive judgment according to revelation, without injustice to appease a hypocrite.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p55/r8.anchor: عرف أن كلها من الله، وأنه ليس للرسول أن يحيد عن شيء منها طلبا لرضا قوم.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p56/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p56/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p56/r1.claim: الكتاب here means the Qurʾān, and بالحق means it contains no crookedness or deviation; الناس is general.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p56/r1.anchor: والكتاب هنا القرآن. ومعنى بالحق: أي لا عوج فيه ولا ميل. والناس هنا عام،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p56/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p56/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p56/r2.claim: The direct sense of بما أراك الله is what God taught through revelation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p56/r2.anchor: وبما أراك الله بما أعلمك من الوحي.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p56/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p56/r3.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p56/r3.claim: One interpretation is sound reasoning, since the Prophet is protected in his independent judgment and infallible in words and deeds.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p56/r3.anchor: وقيل: بالنظر الصحيح فإنه محروس في اجتهاده، معصوم في الأقوال والأفعال.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p56/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p56/r4.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p56/r4.claim: Another interpretation is what God casts into the Prophet's heart through illuminated knowledge and purity of inner perception.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p56/r4.anchor: وقيل: بما ألقاه في قلبك من أنوار المعرفة وصفاء الباطن.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p56/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p56/r5.speaker: عمر
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p56/r5.claim: ʿUmar warns people not to say they judged as God showed them: that assurance belonged only to the Prophet, whose judgment God guided, whereas others rely on conjecture and accountable effort.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p56/r5.anchor: وعن عمر: «لا يقولن أحدكم قضيت بما أراني الله، فإن الله لم يجعل ذلك إلا لنبيه،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p56/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p56/r6.speaker: الماتريدي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p56/r6.claim: Al-Māturīdī offers several senses of بالحق: conforming to duties and mutual rights, explaining God's command, affirming the coming resurrection, imposing liability on its agent, or conveying justice and truth protected from alteration.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p56/r6.anchor: وقال الماتريدي: بالحق أي: موافقا لما هو الحق على العباد، ولما لبعضهم على بعض

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p56/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p56/r7.speaker: الماتريدي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p56/r7.claim: Al-Māturīdī takes the wording as proof that the Prophet may exercise ijtihād and that his judgment is like revealed text, because God shows it to him and does not show him error.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p56/r7.anchor: بما أراك الله: فيه دليل جواز اجتهاده، واجتهاده كالنص، لأن الله تعالى أخبر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p56/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p56/r8.speaker: الزجاج
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p56/r8.claim: Al-Zajjāj, al-Fārisī, and others say خصيما means one who argues, like جليس meaning one who sits with another; it may instead be an intensive form of خصم.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p56/r8.anchor: أي: مخاصما، كجليس بمعنى مجالس، قاله: الزجاج والفارسي وغيرهما.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p56/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p56/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p56/r9.claim: The plural can refer to the three Banū Ubayriq although only one stole: it includes those who vouched for his innocence, especially anyone who knew he was the thief.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p56/r9.anchor: فإن بني أبيرق الثلاثة هم الذين نقبوا المشربة، فظاهر إطلاق الجمع عليهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p56/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p56/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p56/r10.claim: Alternatively, the plural covers Ṭuʿma and anyone who commits such treachery, so no traitor should ever be defended or advocated for.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p56/r10.anchor: أو جاء الجمع ليتناول طعمة وكل من خان خيانته، فلا يخاصم لخائن قط،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p56/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p56/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p56/r11.claim: خصيما has an omitted complement, namely pleading innocence for the accused.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p56/r11.anchor: وخصيما يحتاج متعلقا محذوفا أي البراء.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p56/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p56/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p56/r12.claim: Depending on which occasion account is followed, the innocent person was the Jew Zayd ibn al-Samīn, Abū Malik al-Anṣārī, or Labīd ibn Sahl.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p56/r12.anchor: والبريء مختلف فيه حسب الاختلاف في السبب: أهو اليهودي الذي دفع إليه طعمة الدرع وهو زيد بن السمين،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p61#2/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p61#2/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p61#2/r11.claim: Across the passage Abū Ḥayyān notes metaphors for traveling and turning toward battle, repetitions with differing complements, and matching or near-matching word forms such as يضلوك وما يضلون and علمك وتعلم.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p61#2/r11.anchor: وتضمنت هذه الآيات أنواعا من الفصاحة والبيان والبديع. منها الاستعارة في: وإذا ضربتم في الأرض،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p62/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p62/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p62/r3.claim: The phrases بما أراك الله and ما لم تكن تعلم leave their referents unspecified, creating ambiguity.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p62/r3.anchor: والإبهام في قوله: بما أراك الله وفي: ما لم تكن تعلم.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p62/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p62/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p62/r4.claim: The address names the Prophet but is intended to teach others, since his protection from error prevents him from defending those in the wrong.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p62/r4.anchor: وخطاب عين ويراد به غيره وفي: ولا تكن للخائنين خصيما فإنه صلى الله عليه وسلم محروس بالعصمة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p62/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p62/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p62/r7.claim: Abū Ḥayyān notes ellipsis at several places across the passage.

ALUSI-FULL:v5p138#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p138#3/r1.speaker: قتادة بن النعمان
ALUSI-FULL:v5p138#3/r1.claim: Qatada recounts that Banu Ubayriq were a poor family; Bishr was a hypocritical poet who composed insults against the Companions and falsely attributed them to others.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p138#3/r1.anchor: عن قتادة بن النعمان رضى الله تعالى عنه أنه قال : كان أهل بيت منا

ALUSI-FULL:v5p138#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p138#3/r2.speaker: قتادة بن النعمان
ALUSI-FULL:v5p138#3/r2.claim: Qatada says his uncle Rifa'a stored flour, weapons, and supplies in a room; the room was broken into at night, and the flour and weapons were stolen.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p138#3/r2.anchor: فابتاع عمى رفاعة بن زيد حملا من الدرمك فجعله فى مشربة له

ALUSI-FULL:v5p138#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p138#3/r3.speaker: قتادة بن النعمان
ALUSI-FULL:v5p138#3/r3.claim: The family suspected Banu Ubayriq after seeing their fire, but they blamed the upright Muslim Lubayd; he drew his sword and demanded they identify the thief.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p138#3/r3.anchor: قد رأينا بنى أبيرق قد استوقدوا فى هذه الليلة ولانرى فيما نرى إلا على بعض طعامكم

ALUSI-FULL:v5p138#3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p138#3/r4.speaker: قتادة بن النعمان
ALUSI-FULL:v5p138#3/r4.claim: Qatada sought the Prophet's help recovering the weapons, not the food; the Ubayriq family rallied Usayr ibn Urwa and neighbors, who accused Qatada and his uncle of slandering pious Muslims without proof.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p138#3/r4.anchor: فأتيت رسول الله ( صلى الله عليه و سلم ) فقلت : يارسول الله إن أهل بيت منا أهل جفاء

ALUSI-FULL:v5p139/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p139/r1.speaker: قتادة بن النعمان
ALUSI-FULL:v5p139/r1.claim: Qatada says the Prophet rebuked him for accusing a devout household without evidence; after revelation, the Prophet returned the weapon, and Rifa'a affirmed his sincere faith by dedicating it to God's cause.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p139/r1.anchor: قال قتادة : فأتيت رسول الله ( صلى الله عليه و سلم ) فكلمته فقال

ALUSI-FULL:v5p139/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p139/r2.speaker: حسان بن ثابت
ALUSI-FULL:v5p139/r2.claim: Hassan ibn Thabit satirized Sulafa for sheltering the fugitive Bashir; after hearing the poem, she threw his belongings at al-Abtah and complained that he brought her nothing but trouble.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p139/r2.anchor: إن حسان بن ثابت رضى الله تعالى عنه هجا سلافة فقال

ALUSI-FULL:v5p139/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p139/r3.speaker: السدي
ALUSI-FULL:v5p139/r3.claim: Al-Suddi's alternative account, preferred by al-Tabari, says a Jew entrusted armor to Ta'ma ibn Ubayriq; Ta'ma stole it, hid it in Abu Malik's house, accused Abu Malik, and asked the Prophet to defend him against the Jews, just before revelation exposed the theft.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p139/r3.anchor: عن السدي واختاره الطبري أن يهوديا استودع طعمة بن أبيرق درعا

ALUSI-FULL:v5p139/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p139/r4.speaker: السدي
ALUSI-FULL:v5p139/r4.claim: In al-Suddi's account Ta'ma fled to Mecca as an apostate after exposure, tried to rob his host al-Hajjaj ibn Ilat, was expelled, and died as an unbeliever at Banu Sulaym's lava field.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p139/r4.anchor: فلما فضح الله تعالى طعمة بالقرآن هرب حتى أتى مكة فكفر بعد إسلامه

ALUSI-FULL:v5p139/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p139/r5.speaker: عكرمة
ALUSI-FULL:v5p139/r5.claim: Ikrima gives another fate: a stone struck Ta'ma while he tried to rob al-Hajjaj; later, after he robbed a Quda'a caravan, its members caught and stoned him to death.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p139/r5.anchor: وعن عكرمة أن طعمه لما نزل فيه القرآن ولحق بقريش ورجع عن دينه

ALUSI-FULL:v5p139/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p139/r6.speaker: ابن زيد
ALUSI-FULL:v5p139/r6.claim: Ibn Zayd says Ta'ma died when a house he broke into in Mecca collapsed on him.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p139/r6.anchor: وعن ابن زيد أنه بعد أن لحق بمكة نقب بيتا يسرقه فهدمه الله تعالى عليه فقتله

ALUSI-FULL:v5p139/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p139/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p139/r7.claim: Another version says Ta'ma was expelled, sailed to Jeddah, stole a purse of dinars aboard ship, and was caught and thrown into the sea.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p139/r7.anchor: وقيل : إنه أخرج فركب سفينة إلى جدة فسرق فيها كيسا فيه دنانير فأخذ وألقى في البحر

ALUSI-FULL:v5p140/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p140/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p140/r1.claim: Emphasis signals the ruling's importance; ascribing revelation to the majestic first-person plural magnifies it, and fronting the object draws attention and anticipation.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p140/r1.anchor: في تأكيد الحكم إيذان بالاعتناء بشأنه كما فى إسناد الانزال إلى ضمير العظمة تعظيما لأمر المسند

ALUSI-FULL:v5p140/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p140/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p140/r2.claim: With truth is a circumstantial phrase: God sent the Qur'an down in a state of truth.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p140/r2.anchor: وقوله سبحانه : بالحق فى موضع الحال أى إنا أنزلنا اليك القرآن متلبسا بالحق

ALUSI-FULL:v5p140/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p140/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p140/r3.claim: The Prophet is to judge all people, upright and wicked alike.

ALUSI-FULL:v5p140/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p140/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p140/r4.claim: What God showed you means what He made known and revealed to you.

ALUSI-FULL:v5p140/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p140/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p140/r5.claim: The relative pronoun has an omitted referent and is the first object of araka; the verb comes from ra'a meaning to know, normally one-object but causativized here to two.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p140/r5.anchor: و ( ما موصولة والعائد محذوف وهو المفعول الأول لأرى

ALUSI-FULL:v5p140/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p140/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p140/r6.claim: Taking the verb as opinion, like al-Shafi'i held this, would make it a cognitive verb needing three objects with two omitted; al-Alusi calls this remote, and a metaphorical inner sight is unnecessary.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p140/r6.anchor: وقيل : إنها من الرأى من قولهم : رأى الشافعى كذا وجعلها علمية يقتضى التعدى إلى ثلاثة

ALUSI-FULL:v5p140/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p140/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p140/r7.claim: The traitors are the Banu Ubayriq or Ta'ma, the person intended by the warning, or anyone who follows their conduct.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p140/r7.anchor: وهم بنو أبيرق أوطعمة ومن يعنيه أو هو ومن يسير بسيرته

ALUSI-FULL:v5p140/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p140/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p140/r8.claim: The preposition can mean for their sake, or alternatively away from or concerning them.

ALUSI-FULL:v5p140/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p140/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p140/r9.claim: An advocate here means someone arguing against innocent people.

ALUSI-FULL:v5p140/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p140/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p140/r10.claim: The prohibition most naturally follows an omitted command to judge by the Book; alternatives coordinate it with We sent down by supplying We said, or with the Book because the prohibition was also revealed, but the latter is far from the apparent construction.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p140/r10.anchor: والنهى معطوف على مقدر ينسحب عليه النظم الكريم كأنه قيل : إنا أنزلنا اليك الكتاب فاحكم به

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p283/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p283/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p283/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas reports that an Ansari, Thaʿma ibn Ubayriq, stole armor from his neighbor Qatada ibn al-Nuʿman, hid it with the Jewish man Zayd al-Samin, and denied the theft under oath; the flour trail led investigators to his house and then to the Jew, who said Thaʿma had given it to him.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p283/r1.anchor: روى الكلبي عن أبي صالح عن ابن عباس قال: نزلت هذه الآية

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p283/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p283/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p283/r2.claim: In the same report, Thaʿma’s clansmen asked the Prophet to defend him lest he be disgraced, and he was about to punish the Jewish man.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p283/r2.anchor: فجاء بنو ظفر وهم قوم طعمة إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وسألوه أن يجادل عن صاحبهم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p283/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p283/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
