BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p283/r3.claim: A second report from Ibn ʿAbbas says Thaʿma left a leaking bran sack at Zayd’s door after taking the armor home; following the bran trail, the owner brought Zayd to the Prophet, who was about to cut the Jew’s hand.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p283/r3.anchor: ويروى عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في رواية أخرى أن طعمة سرق الدرع في جراب فيه نخالة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p283/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p283/r4.speaker: مقاتل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p283/r4.claim: Muqatil gives a different account: Zayd had entrusted armor to Thaʿma, who then denied possessing it, and the verse was revealed.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p283/r4.anchor: وقال مقاتل: إن زيدا السمين أودع درعا عند طعمة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p283/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p283/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p283/r5.claim: The Book was sent with commands, prohibitions, and decisive judgment.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p283/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p283/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p283/r6.claim: The Prophet is to judge by what God taught him and revealed to him.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p283/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p283/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p283/r7.claim: The treacherous person is Thaʿma, and the command forbids acting as his advocate or defender.

BAYDAWI-FULL:4:105/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:105/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:105/r1.claim: The occasion was Tuʿma ibn Ubayriq of Banu Ẓafar stealing a coat of mail from neighbor Qatada ibn al-Nuʿman in a leaky flour sack, hiding it with the Jew Zayd ibn al-Samin, and denying the theft; flour led investigators to Zayd, who said Tuʿma gave it to him and was backed by Jewish witnesses. Banu Ẓafar urged the Prophet to defend Tuʿma against the innocent Jew, and he nearly did.
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:105/r1.anchor: نزلت في طعمة بن أبيرق من بني ظفر، سرق درعا من جاره قتادة بن النعمان في جراب دقيق، فجعل الدقيق ينتثر من خرق فيه وخبأها عند زيد بن السمين اليهودي، فالتمست الدرع عند طعمة فلم توجد، وحلف ما أخذها وماله بها علم فتركوه واتبعوا أثر الدقيق حتى انتهى إلى منزل اليهودي فأخذوها. فقال دفعها إلى طعمة وشهد له ناس من اليهود فقالت بنو ظفر: انطلقوا بنا إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فسألوه أن يجادل عن صاحبهم وقالوا: إن لم تفعل هلك وافتضح وبرىء اليهودي فهم رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أن يفعل

BAYDAWI-FULL:4:105/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:105/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:105/r2.claim: “What God showed you” means what He made known and revealed to you, not “made you know”: that sense of raʾā would require three objects.
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:105/r2.anchor: بما عرفك الله وأوحى به إليك وليس من الرؤية بمعنى العلم وإلا لاستدعى ثلاثة مفاعيل

BAYDAWI-FULL:4:105/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:105/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:105/r3.claim: Do not argue on behalf of the betrayers or defend them against the innocent.
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:105/r3.anchor: أي لأجلهم والذب عنهم { خصيما } للبرآء

BIQAI-FULL:v2p310#2/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p310#2/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p310#2/r1.claim: After discussing the People of the Book, their misguidance, and the hypocrites' preference for another judgment, this verse aptly states that the Book was sent in truth for judgment.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p310#2/r1.anchor: وساق سبحانه وتعالى أصول ذلك وفروعه

BIQAI-FULL:v2p310#2/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p310#2/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p310#2/r2.claim: The Prophet is to judge all people because his call is universal; those who abandon his judgment and seek better guidance outside the Book are most astray.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p310#2/r2.anchor: لأن دعوتك عامة فلا أضل ممن عدل عن حكمك

BIQAI-FULL:v2p310#2/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p310#2/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p310#2/r3.claim: God's showing the judgment means the Prophet does not speak from whim: he should act when God has made a matter clear and wait for clarification otherwise.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p310#2/r3.anchor: إن كان قد بين لك شيئا غاية البيان فافعله

BIQAI-FULL:v2p310#2/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p310#2/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p310#2/r4.claim: The occasion involved Tu'ma ibn Ubayriq stealing armor and leaving it with a Jew; when found with the Jew, he claimed Tu'ma had deposited it, and the theft was not established against Tu'ma until the revelation.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p310#2/r4.anchor: سرق درعا وأودعها عند يهودي , فوجدت عنده

BIQAI-FULL:v2p310#2/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p310#2/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p310#2/r5.claim: God eased the Prophet's task by requiring judgment on outward evidence rather than investigation of hidden states; the case was ambiguous and involved defending Tu'ma.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p310#2/r5.anchor: قد خفف عليه صلى الله عليه وسلم بأن شرع له القناعة في الحكم بالظاهر وعدم التكليف بالنقب

BIQAI-FULL:v2p310#2/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p310#2/r6.speaker: الجمهور
BIQAI-FULL:v2p310#2/r6.claim: The author calls it the sound view, citing Ibn Hajar, that al-Khidr was a prophet; Muhammad was given all prophets' miracles plus what was uniquely his.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p310#2/r6.anchor: الجمهور - كما نقله شيخنا قاضي الشافعية بمصر أبو الفضل أحمد بنعلي بن حجر

BIQAI-FULL:v2p310#2/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p310#2/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p310#2/r7.claim: The prohibition means not to act as an advocate for traitors such as Tu'ma.

BIQAI-FULL:v2p310#2/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p310#2/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p310#2/r8.claim: The command follows the discussion of judging by what God reveals, introducing further exposure of the opponents' hidden traits so believers can recognize and avoid them.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p310#2/r8.anchor: ثم شرع سبحانه وتعالى في إتمام ما بقي من أخبارهم

DURR-FULL:v2p670/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p670/r1.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v2p670/r1.claim: Qatada recounts that Banu Ubayriq accused the upright Lubayd ibn Sahl of stealing after breaking into Rifa'a ibn Zayd's storeroom; Lubayd confronted them, and Qatada asked the Prophet to recover his uncle's weapons.
DURR-FULL:v2p670/r1.anchor: قال قتادة: فأتيت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقلت: يا رسول الله إن أهل بيت منا أهل جفاء عمدوا إلى عمي

DURR-FULL:v2p670/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p670/r2.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v2p670/r2.claim: Qatada says Banu Ubayriq enlisted Asir ibn Urwa and others to portray the accusation as baseless; the Prophet reproached Qatada, who regretted speaking, then revelation condemned the defense of the traitors and their false accusation of Lubayd.
DURR-FULL:v2p670/r2.anchor: فقالوا: يا رسول الله إن قتادة بن النعمان وعمه عمدوا إلى أهل بيت منا أهل إسلام وصلاح

DURR-FULL:v2p675/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p675/r1.speaker: author
DURR-FULL:v2p675/r1.claim: In this account, Ta'ma's allies among the Ansar ask Muhammad to defend him and discredit the Jewish accuser; revelation checks that defense, condemns their private plotting, and exposes Ta'ma, who flees to Mecca and apostatizes.
DURR-FULL:v2p675/r1.anchor: من الأنصار فقالوا: يا رسول الله جادل عن طعمة وأكذب اليهودي

DURR-FULL:v2p675/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p675/r3.speaker: عكرمة
DURR-FULL:v2p675/r3.claim: Ikrima says an Ansari entrusted Ta'ma ibn Ubayriq with armor; Ta'ma stole it, blamed the Jew Zayd ibn al-Samin, and enlisted his people to plead before the Prophet, who was inclined to shield him before revelation exposed the lie.
DURR-FULL:v2p675/r3.anchor: عن عكرمة قال: استودع رجل من الأنصار طعمة بن أبيرق مشربة له فيها درع

DURR-FULL:v2p676/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p676/r2.speaker: الضحاك
DURR-FULL:v2p676/r2.claim: Al-Dahhak says an Ansari denied keeping entrusted armor; the Prophet initially defended him as apparently innocent after his relatives pleaded, but revelation exposed his betrayal, after which he fled to Mecca and apostatized.
DURR-FULL:v2p676/r2.anchor: وأخرج ابن جرير عن الضحاك قال: نزلت هذه الآية في رجل من الأنصار استودع درعا فجحدها

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1058#2/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1058#2/r1.speaker: ربيعة
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1058#2/r1.claim: Rabīʿa says God revealed the Qur'an while leaving room for the Sunnah, and the Messenger established the Sunnah while leaving room for legal reasoning.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1058#2/r1.anchor: عن ربيعة قال : ان الله تبارك وتعالى انزل القران وترك فيه موضعا للسنة

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1058#2/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1058#2/r2.speaker: مالك
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1058#2/r2.claim: Mālik distinguishes judgment by Qur'an and established Sunnah as binding and correct, qualified reasoning where no text exists as potentially correct, and presumptuous judgment without knowledge as unlikely to succeed.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1058#2/r2.anchor: قال لي مالك : الحكم الذي يحكم به بين الناس على وجهين

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1058#2/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1058#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1058#2/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās warns against personal opinion, noting that God commanded the Prophet to judge by what He showed him, not by what the Prophet himself saw.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1058#2/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال : اياكم والراي ، قال الله تعالى لنبيه احكم بينهم بما اراك الله

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1058#2/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1058#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1058#2/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains what God showed the Prophet as what He revealed to him of the Book.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1058#2/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس قوله : بما اراك الله يقول : بما انزل الله اليك من الكتاب .

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1058#2/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1058#2/r5.speaker: عطية
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1058#2/r5.claim: ʿAṭiyya says God showed His Book to the Prophet.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1058#2/r5.anchor: عن عطية لتحكم بين الناس بما اراك الله قال : النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم اراه الله كتابه .

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1058#2/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1058#2/r6.speaker: مطر
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1058#2/r6.claim: Maṭar says the Prophet judges between people by clear proofs and witnesses.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1058#2/r6.anchor: عن مطر في قوله : لتحكم بين الناس بما اراك الله قال : بالبينات والشهود .

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1058#2/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1058#2/r7.speaker: قتادة بن النعمان
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1058#2/r7.claim: Qatāda b. al-Nuʿmān recounts asking the Prophet about a household that broke into his uncle Rifāʿa's storehouse and took weapons and food; the passage ends as the accused household responds by accusing Qatāda and his uncle.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1058#2/r7.anchor: عن جده قتادة بن النعمان قال : اتيت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ، فقلت : يا رسول الله ، ان اهل بيت منا

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1060/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1060/r1.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1060/r1.claim: Qatāda recounts the Banū Ubayriq theft case: the Prophet rebuked an accusation made without proof; after revelation, the weapon was returned to his uncle.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1060/r1.anchor: قال قتادة : فاتيت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فكلمته ، فقال : عمدت إلى اهل بيت ذكر منهم اسلام وصلاح

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p40/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p40/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p40/r1.claim: One purpose of revelation is moral refinement; the Prophet's character was the Qur'an.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p40/r1.anchor: رضي الله تعالى عنها لما سئلت عن خلقه صلى الله عليه وسلم فقالت كان خلقه القرآن

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p40/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p40/r2.speaker: عائشة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p40/r2.claim: When asked about the Prophet's character, Aisha answered that his character was the Qur'an.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p40/r2.anchor: رضي الله تعالى عنها لما سئلت عن خلقه صلى الله عليه وسلم فقالت كان خلقه القرآن

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p40/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p40/r3.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p40/r3.claim: Malik transmits as a balagh in al-Muwatta the Prophet's statement that he was sent to perfect noble character.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p40/r3.anchor: وفي الحديث الذي رواه مالك في الموطأ بلاغا أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال بعثت لأتمم مكارم حسن الأخلاق

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p40/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p40/r4.speaker: أبو خراش الهذلي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p40/r4.claim: Abu Khirash al-Hudhali's poem says Islam's restraints encircled people's necks and made the young man behave like an old man, speaking only justice.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p40/r4.anchor: وقال أبو خراش الهذلي مشيرا إلى ما دخل على العرب من أحكام الإسلام بأحسن تعبير

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p40/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p40/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p40/r5.claim: Legislation, both specific and general rulings, is another purpose of revelation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p40/r5.anchor: الثالث : التشريع وهو الأحكام خاصة وعامة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p40/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p40/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p40/r6.claim: The Qur'an gives most rulings as universal principles and supplies detailed rulings in matters of importance.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p40/r6.anchor: ولقد جمع القرآن جميع الأحكام جمعا كليا في الغالب ، وجزئيا في المهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p40/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p40/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p40/r7.claim: The completion of religion means completion of its universal principles, including the directive to derive rulings and use analogy.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p40/r7.anchor: المراد بهما إكمال الكليات التي منها الأمر بالاستنباط والقياس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p40/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p40/r8.speaker: الشاطبي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p40/r8.claim: Al-Shatibi argues that the Qur'an's concise comprehensiveness contains the universal principles needed for the completed law.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p40/r8.anchor: قال الشاطبي لأنه على اختصاره جامع والشريعة تمت بتمامه ولا يكون جامعا لتمام الدين إلا والمجموع فيه أمور كلية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p40/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p40/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p40/r9.claim: A further purpose is the governance of the community and preservation of its order, through unity, avoiding faction and conflict, and consultation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p40/r9.anchor: الرابع : سياسة الأمة وهو باب عظيم في القرآن القصد منه صلاح الأمة وحفظ نظامها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p40/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p40/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p40/r10.claim: Stories of earlier peoples teach by presenting good examples to emulate, bad examples to avoid, and lessons within the narratives.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p40/r10.anchor: الخامس : القصص وأخبار الأمم السالفة للتأسي بصالح أحوالهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p40/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p40/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p40/r11.claim: The Qur'an educates people in ways suited to their era and prepares them to receive and spread the law, building on the scriptural and historical learning familiar to Arabs.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p40/r11.anchor: السادس : التعليم بما يناسب حالة عصر المخاطبين ، وما يؤهلهم إلى تلقي الشريعة ونشرها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p40/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p40/r12.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p40/r12.claim: It also teaches sound reasoning and inference through debates and calls to reflection, and honors wisdom as a source of broad knowledge.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p40/r12.anchor: وقد زاد القرآن على ذلك تعليم حكمة ميزان العقول وصحة الاستدلال في أفانين مجادلاته للضالين وفي دعوته إلى النظر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p40/r13.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p40/r13.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p40/r13.claim: The Qur'an repeatedly emphasizes knowledge, a new emphasis for Arabs whose learning was largely empirical and whose sages were rare; it also points to the value of writing.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p40/r13.anchor: إنما قصارى علومهم أمور تجريبية ، وكان حكماؤهم أفرادا اختصوا بفرط ذكاء تضم إليه تجربة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p40/r14.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p40/r14.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p40/r14.claim: Another purpose is exhortation, warning, caution, and good news, including promises, threats, and argument with the defiant.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p40/r14.anchor: السابع : المواعظ والإنذار والتحذير والتبشير ، وهذا يجمع جميع آيات الوعد والوعيد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p40/r15.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p40/r15.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p40/r15.claim: The Qur'an's inimitability is a sign of the Messenger's truth after challenge; it is miraculous in wording and challenged through its meaning.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p40/r15.anchor: الثامن : الإعجاز بالقرآن ليكون آية دالة على صدق الرسول ؛ إذ التصديق يتوقف على دلالة المعجزة بعد التحدي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p40/r16.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p40/r16.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p40/r16.claim: Knowing occasions of revelation helps clarify the rhetorical situation relevant to the Qur'anic challenge.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p40/r16.anchor: ولمعرفة أسباب النزول مدخل في ظهور مقتضى الحال ووضوحه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p40/r17.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p40/r17.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p40/r17.claim: Ibn Ashur says this is the extent of his survey and notes that al-Ghazali discusses some of these purposes in Ihya Ulum al-Din.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p40/r17.anchor: هذا ما بلغ إليه استقرائي . وللغزالي في أحياء علوم الدين بعض من ذلك

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p108#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p108#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p108#2/r1.claim: The verse honors and entrusts judgment to the Prophet, while correcting his judgment and reproaching him for initially accepting the report about Banu Ubayriq too quickly.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p108#2/r1.anchor: في هذه الآية تشريف للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وتفويض إليه، وتقويم أيضا على الجادة في الحكم، وتأنيب ما على قبول ما رفع إليه في أمر بني أبيرق بسرعة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p108#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p108#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p108#2/r2.claim: Judging by what God showed means judging according to the law, through revelation and explicit text or reasoned judgment following revelation's way.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p108#2/r2.anchor: بما أراك الله معناه: على قوانين الشرع، إما بوحي ونص، أو بنظر جار على سنن الوحي

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p108#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p108#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p108#2/r3.claim: God guarantees that His prophets are protected from error in this matter.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p108#2/r3.anchor: وقد تضمن الله تعالى لأنبيائه العصمة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p108#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p108#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p108#2/r4.claim: Exegetes agree that the warning and command to seek forgiveness arose from the Banu Ubayriq case.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p108#2/r4.anchor: سببها باتفاق من المتأولين أمر بني أبيرق

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p108#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p108#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p108#2/r5.claim: In this account, Bashir of the Ubayriq brothers was a hypocrite who mocked the Companions and falsely attributed others' poetry to them; one poem complained that men's poems were ascribed to Ibn al-Ubayriq.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p108#2/r5.anchor: وكان بشير رجلا منافقا يهجو أصحاب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p108#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p108#2/r6.speaker: قتادة بن النعمان
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p108#2/r6.claim: Qatada reports that his uncle Rifa'a's food, two armors, and two swords were stolen from a storeroom; suspicion fell on the impoverished Banu Ubayriq after they lit a fire that night.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p108#2/r6.anchor: فابتاع عمي رفاعة بن زيد حملا من دومك الشام فجعله في مشربة له

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p108#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p108#2/r7.speaker: قتادة بن النعمان
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p108#2/r7.claim: Qatada recounts that the Ubayriq brothers diverted suspicion to the upright Labid ibn Sahl, who confronted them with his sword; Qatada then told the Prophet, who initially rebuked him for accusing a righteous Muslim without proof.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p108#2/r7.anchor: والله ما نرى صاحبكم إلا لبيد بن سهل، رجل منا له صلاح وإسلام

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p108#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p108#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p108#2/r8.claim: In the account just related, the traitors are Banu Ubayriq, the innocent man framed is Labid ibn Sahl, and the plotting group is Usayr and his companions.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p108#2/r8.anchor: فالخائنون بنو أبيرق، والبريء المرمي لبيد بن سهل، والطائفة التي همت: أسير وأصحابه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p109/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p109/r1.speaker: قتادة وغير واحد من المتأولين
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p109/r1.claim: Qatada and other interpreters identify the culprit in the case as Ta'ma ibn Ubayriq, also called Tu'ayma.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p109/r1.anchor: وقال قتادة وغير واحد من المتأولين: هذه القصة ونحوها إنما كان صاحبها طعمة بن أبيرق

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p109/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p109/r2.speaker: السدي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p109/r2.claim: Al-Suddi says Ta'ma denied stealing armor entrusted to him by a Jew, hid it in Abu Malil al-Ansari's house, and tried to frame Abu Malil when exposed; Abu Malil was innocent.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p109/r2.anchor: وقال السدي: القصة في طعمة بن أبيرق لكن بأن استودعه يهودي درعا فجحده إياها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p109/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p109/r3.speaker: عكرمة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p109/r3.claim: Ikrima says Ta'ma stole armor from a storeroom and accused a Jew named Zayd ibn al-Samin of the theft.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p109/r3.anchor: وقال عكرمة: سرق طعمة بن أبيرق درعا من مشربة ورمى بسرقتها رجلا من اليهود

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p109/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p109/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p109/r4.claim: The shared substance is that Ta'ma's people petitioned the Prophet to defend him and withdraw the charge, although some knew he had stolen; believing members sinned, hypocrites acted deliberately, and God protected His Messenger.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p109/r4.anchor: وجملة هذا يستدير على أن قوم طعمة أتوا النبي وكلموه في أن يذب عن طعمة ويرفع الدعوى عنه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p109/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p109/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p109/r5.claim: The author says Ta'ima later apostatized and fled to Mecca; after Sulafa received Hassan ibn Thabit's poem about him, she expelled him and threw out his belongings.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p109/r5.anchor: وطعيمة بن أبيرق صرح بعد ذلك بالارتداد وهرب إلى مكة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p109/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p109/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p109/r6.claim: Other reports give different endings for Ta'ma: Hajjaj ibn Allat expelled him after a theft, a collapsing wall killed him while burgling, or Arabs killed him after he robbed them.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p109/r6.anchor: فروي: أنه نزل على الحجاج بن علاط وسرقه فطرده، وروي أنه نقب حائط بيت ليسرقه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p190/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p190/r1.speaker: أبو صالح عن ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p190/r1.claim: Abu Salih reports from Ibn Abbas that Taʿma ibn Ubayriq stole Qatada ibn al-Nuʿman's armor, hid it at a Jew's home after flour leaking from its bag marked the trail, and denied the theft. His people urged the Prophet to defend him; the Prophet nearly did so and punish the Jew when the verses came down.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p190/r1.anchor: أحدها أن طعمة بن أبيرق سرق درعا لقتادة بن النعمان وكان الدرع في جراب فيه دقيق

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p190/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p190/r2.speaker: السدي، مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p190/r2.claim: Al-Suddi and Muqatil say a Jew entrusted armor to Taʿma, who betrayed the trust and hid it in Abu Mulayl al-Ansari's home; Taʿma's people asked the Prophet to exonerate him and discredit the Jew.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p190/r2.anchor: والثاني أن رجلا من اليهود استودع طعمة بن أبيرق درعا فخانها فلما خاف اطلاعهم عليها ألقاها

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p190/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p190/r3.speaker: قتادة بن النعمان
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p190/r3.claim: Qatada ibn al-Nuʿman says Rifaʿa ibn Zayd's storeroom was broken into and food and weapons stolen; Banu Ubayriq's three men were suspected, but their kinsmen accused Qatada of slandering a pious Muslim household. The Prophet rebuked his accusation as unsupported, and the verses came down.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p190/r3.anchor: والثالث أن مشربة رفاعة بن زيد نقبت وأخذ طعامه وسلاحه فاتهم به بنو أبيرق وكانوا ثلاثة بشير ومبشر

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p190/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p190/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p190/r5.claim: Al-ḥaqq here means judgment with justice.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p190/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p190/r6.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p190/r6.claim: Taḥkuma bayna al-nās means to judge between the people.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p190/r6.anchor: ﴿ لتحكم بين الناس ﴾ أي لتقضي بينهم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p191/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p191/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p191/r1.claim: One reading is that God taught the Prophet to accept no one's claim against another without proof.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p191/r1.anchor: أحدهما أنه الذي علمه والذي علمه أن لا يقبل دعوى أحد على أحد إلا ببرهان

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p191/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p191/r2.speaker: الماوردي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p191/r2.claim: A second view, mentioned by al-Mawardi, is that judgment follows what the Prophet's independent reasoning leads him to.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p191/r2.anchor: والثاني أنه ما يؤدي إليه اجتهاده ذكره الماوردي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p191/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p191/r3.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p191/r3.claim: Al-Zajjaj explains the command as “do not litigate for or defend a traitor.”
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p191/r3.anchor: قال الزجاج لا تكن مخاصما ولا دافعا عن خائن واختلفوا هل خاصم عنه أم لا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p191/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p191/r4.speaker: العوفي عن ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p191/r4.claim: One view says the Prophet did argue for the traitor, rising to address people in his defense.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p191/r4.anchor: أحدهما أنه قام خطيبا فعذره رواه العوفي عن ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p191/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p191/r5.speaker: سعيد بن جبير، قتادة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p191/r5.claim: Another view says the Prophet only intended to defend him and did not do so.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p191/r5.anchor: والثاني أنه هم بذلك ولم يفعله قاله سعيد بن جبير وقتادة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p191/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p191/r6.speaker: القاضي أبو يعلى
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p191/r6.claim: Al-Qadi Abu Yaʿla infers that no one may litigate to establish or deny another's right without knowing the facts, since God reproached the Prophet for such conduct.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p191/r6.anchor: وهذه الآية تدل على أنه لا يجوز لأحد أن يخاصم عن غيره في إثبات حق أو نفيه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p404#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p404#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p404#2/r1.claim: The revealed Book is true from God and contains truth in both its reports and its commands.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p404#2/r1.anchor: أي: هو حق من الله، وهو يتضمن الحق في خبره وطلبه.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p404#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p404#2/r2.speaker: علماء الأصول
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p404#2/r2.claim: Some legal theorists cite this verse as proof that the Prophet could decide cases through ijtihād.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p404#2/r2.anchor: احتج به من ذهب من علماء الأصول إلى أنه كان، عليه السلام، له أن يحكم بالاجتهاد بهذه الآية

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p404#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p404#2/r3.speaker: أم سلمة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p404#2/r3.claim: In a report in both Ṣaḥīḥ collections, Umm Salama says the Prophet warned disputants that he judges from what he hears, so a more persuasive but undeserving claimant may receive another Muslim's right as a portion of fire.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p404#2/r3.anchor: عن أم سلمة؛ أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم سمع حلبة خصم بباب حجرته، فخرج إليهم فقال: "ألا إنما أنا بشر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p404#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p404#2/r4.speaker: أم سلمة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p404#2/r4.claim: In another report, two Ansar disputed an old inheritance without evidence; the Prophet warned against taking a brother's right, and they agreed to divide it, seek the truth, draw lots, and release each other.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p404#2/r4.anchor: عن أم سلمة قالت: جاء رجلان من الأنصار يختصمان إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في مواريث بينهما قد درست

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p404#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p404#2/r5.speaker: أبو داود
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p404#2/r5.claim: Abū Dāwūd's version adds that the Prophet judged between them by opinion concerning a matter on which no revelation had come to him.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p404#2/r5.anchor: وقد رواه أبو داود من حديث أسامة بن زيد، به.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p405/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p405/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p405/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that Ṭuʿmah b. Ubairiq hid a stolen shield in an innocent man's home and his clan sought public defense for him; the revelation exposed the theft and condemned advocacy for the treacherous.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p405/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: إن نفرا من الأنصار غزوا مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في بعض غزواته، فسرقت درع لأحدهم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p405/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p405/r2.speaker: مجاهد، وعكرمة، وقتادة، والسدي، وابن زيد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p405/r2.claim: Mujāhid, ʿIkrimah, Qatādah, al-Suddī, Ibn Zayd, and others likewise say the verses were revealed about the Banu Ubairiq thief, with related but varying accounts.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p405/r2.anchor: ذكر مجاهد، وعكرمة، وقتادة، والسدي، وابن زيد وغيرهم في هذه الآية

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p405/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p405/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p405/r3.claim: Ibn Kathīr calls the Ibn ʿAbbās account an unusual narrative.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p405/r3.anchor: يعني: السارق والذين جادلوا عن السارق. وهذا سياق غريب

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p405#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p405#2/r1.speaker: قتادة بن النعمان
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p405#2/r1.claim: Qatādah b. al-Nuʿmān says the poor Banu Ubairiq included Bishr, Bashīr, and Mubashshir; Bashīr was a hypocritical poet, and after Rifāʿa's stored flour and arms were stolen, they falsely blamed the upright Lubayd b. Sahl.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p405#2/r1.anchor: عن أبيه، عن جده قتادة بن النعمان، رضي الله عنه، قال: كان أهل بيت منا يقال لهم بنو أبيرق: بشر وبشير ومبشر، وكان بشير رجلا منافقا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p406/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p406/r1.speaker: قتادة بن النعمان
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p406/r1.claim: Qatādah asked the Prophet to recover the stolen arms; after members of the neighborhood defended the accused household, the Prophet reproached the accusation without proof, and revelation exposed the plot and prohibited defending the self-betrayers.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p406/r1.anchor: قال قتادة: فأتيت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فكلمته، فقال: "عمدت إلى أهل بيت ذكر منهم إسلام وصلاح، ترميهم بالسرقة على غير ثبت ولا بينة؟

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p406/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p406/r2.speaker: قتادة بن النعمان
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p406/r2.claim: The Prophet returned the arms; Qatādah's uncle dedicated them to God's path, confirming his sincere faith. Bashīr then joined the polytheists; verses condemning opposition to the Messenger followed, and Ḥassān's satire led Sulāfa to throw out his belongings.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p406/r2.anchor: فقال قتادة: لما أتيت عمي بالسلاح وكان شيخا، قد عشا أو عسا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p407/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p407/r1.speaker: الترمذي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p407/r1.claim: Al-Tirmidhī calls the report gharīb and says he knows no connected chain for it besides Muḥammad b. Salamah; Yūnus b. Bukayr and others transmit it mursal, omitting Qatādah's father and grandfather.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p407/r1.anchor: ثم قال الترمذي: هذا حديث غريب لا نعلم أحدا أسنده غير محمد بن سلمة الحراني

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p407/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p407/r2.speaker: الحاكم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p407/r2.claim: Al-Ḥākim grades the report ṣaḥīḥ according to Muslim's criteria, though neither Muslim nor al-Bukhārī included it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p407/r2.anchor: ثم قال: وهذا حديث صحيح على شرط مسلم، ولم يخرجاه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p6/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p6/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p6/r1.claim: Ibn Kathīr condemns earlier People of the Book for neglecting their scripture in favor of worldly accumulation and urges Muslims to learn, teach, understand, and explain the revelation given to them.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p6/r1.anchor: فذم الله تعالى أهل الكتاب قبلنا بإعراضهم عن كتاب الله إليهم، وإقبالهم على الدنيا وجمعها

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p6/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p6/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p6/r2.claim: Ibn Kathīr links God’s promise to revive dead earth with softening hearts through faith after sin and hardness, citing 57:16–17 as a warning and encouragement to believers.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p6/r2.anchor: كما يحيي الأرض بعد موتها، كذلك يلين القلوب بالإيمان بعد قسوتها من الذنوب والمعاصي

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p6/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p6/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p6/r3.claim: The soundest tafsīr method is to explain the Qurʾan by the Qurʾan, then by the Sunna, which clarifies it; al-Shāfiʿī says every ruling of the Prophet was understood from the Qurʾan.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p6/r3.anchor: إن أصح الطرق في ذلك أن يفسر القرآن بالقرآن، فما أجمل في مكان فإنه قد فسر في موضع آخر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p6/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p6/r4.speaker: الشافعي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p6/r4.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī says everything the Messenger ruled was something he had understood from the Qurʾan; Ibn Kathīr supports the method with verses assigning the Prophet the task of explaining revelation.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p6/r4.anchor: قال الإمام أبو عبد الله محمد بن إدريس الشافعي، رحمه الله: كل ما حكم به رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p6/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p6/r5.speaker: النبي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p6/r5.claim: The Prophet says he was given the Qurʾan and something like it along with it; Ibn Kathīr identifies the latter as the Sunna and says the Sunna too comes by revelation, though it is not recited like the Qurʾan.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p6/r5.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "ألا إني أوتيت القرآن ومثله معه" (1) يعني: السنة

JISHUMI:v3p1729/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p1729/r12.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v3p1729/r12.claim: Truth is putting a thing in its proper place as wisdom requires.
JISHUMI:v3p1729/r12.anchor: الحق: وضع الشيء موضعه على ما تقضيه الحكمة

JISHUMI:v3p1729/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p1729/r13.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v3p1729/r13.claim: As an attribute of God, al-Haqq means the possessor of right; for the Book it can mean possessing truth or being set according to wisdom.
JISHUMI:v3p1729/r13.anchor: ويقال لله تعالى الحق، أي ذو الحق، وفي الكتاب أنه حق معنيان

JISHUMI:v3p1729/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p1729/r14.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v3p1729/r14.claim: مخاصمة means dispute; خصم works for singular or plural and for masculine or feminine, while خصام is the verbal noun of خاصم.
JISHUMI:v3p1729/r14.anchor: والمخاصمة: المنازعة، والخصم يستوي فيه الواحد والجمع والذكر والأنثى

JISHUMI:v3p1729/r15.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p1729/r15.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v3p1729/r15.claim: A traitor is the opposite of a trustworthy person; the root sense of betrayal is deficiency or taking away.
JISHUMI:v3p1729/r15.anchor: والخائن: ضد الأمين، وأصله الخيانة، وأصله النقصان

JISHUMI:v3p1729/r16.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p1729/r16.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v3p1729/r16.claim: The preposition ب can attach to أنزل, meaning God sent the Book down in truth; another parsing says it descended upon truth and made truth clear.
JISHUMI:v3p1729/r16.anchor: الباء في قوله: بالحق يعني أنزل. على وجه الحق، وقيل: نزل على الحق

JISHUMI:v3p1729/r17.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p1729/r17.speaker: السدي والضحاك
JISHUMI:v3p1729/r17.claim: They say the verse concerned Tuʿma ibn Ubayriq, who denied keeping a deposited coat of mail; his relatives defended him without proof, and the Prophet nearly sided with them before revelation exposed the case.
JISHUMI:v3p1729/r17.anchor: نزلت الآية في درع كانت وديعة

JISHUMI:v3p1729/r18.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p1729/r18.speaker: الحسن وابن زيد
JISHUMI:v3p1729/r18.claim: They say Tuʿma stole a coat of mail and his relatives argued on his behalf.
JISHUMI:v3p1729/r18.anchor: وقيل: إنه سرق درعا فجادل عنه قومه عن الحسن وابن زيد

JISHUMI:v3p1729/r19.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p1729/r19.speaker: قتادة بن النعمان
JISHUMI:v3p1729/r19.claim: Qatada recounts how Banu Ubayriq stole food and weapons from Rifaʿa ibn Zayd, blamed the righteous Muslim Lubayd, and accused Qatada when he reported them; revelation identified the traitors, and Bishr later fled to the polytheists.
JISHUMI:v3p1729/r19.anchor: وعن قتادة بن النعمان قال: كان أهل بيت منا يقال لهم بنو أبيرق

TIRMIDHI:3036/r1.author: TIRMIDHI
TIRMIDHI:3036/r1.speaker: قتادة بن النعمان
TIRMIDHI:3036/r1.claim: Qatada describes the poor Banu Ubayriq household and says Bashir was a hypocritical poet who composed satire against the Prophet’s Companions and passed it off as others’ work.
TIRMIDHI:3036/r1.anchor: قتادة بن النعمان قال كان أهل بيت منا يقال لهم بنو أبيرق بشر وبشير ومبشر وكان بشير رجلا منافقا يقول الشعر يهجو به أصحاب رسول

TIRMIDHI:3036/r2.author: TIRMIDHI
TIRMIDHI:3036/r2.speaker: قتادة بن النعمان
TIRMIDHI:3036/r2.claim: Rifaʿa b. Zayd’s store was broken into and food and weapons stolen; the household was suspected, while its members blamed Labid, a righteous Muslim, and denied the theft.
TIRMIDHI:3036/r2.anchor: قال قتادة فأتيت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقلت إن أهل بيت منا أهل جفاء عمدوا

TIRMIDHI:3036/r3.author: TIRMIDHI
TIRMIDHI:3036/r3.speaker: قتادة بن النعمان
TIRMIDHI:3036/r3.claim: After the Prophet rebuked Qatada for accusing a household known for piety without proof, revelation identified Banu Ubayriq as the traitors and ordered judgment by what God revealed rather than advocacy for them.
TIRMIDHI:3036/r3.anchor: قال قتادة فأتيت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقلت إن أهل بيت منا أهل جفاء عمدوا

TIRMIDHI:3036/r6.author: TIRMIDHI
TIRMIDHI:3036/r6.speaker: قتادة بن النعمان
TIRMIDHI:3036/r6.claim: After the revelation, the Prophet returned the weapons to Rifaʿa; when Rifaʿa dedicated them to God’s path, Qatada recognized that his uncle’s Islam was sound.
TIRMIDHI:3036/r6.anchor: قال قتادة لما أتيت عمي بالسلاح وكان شيخا قد عسى أو عشي في الجاهلية وكنت أرى إسلامه مدخولا

TIRMIDHI:3036/r8.author: TIRMIDHI
TIRMIDHI:3036/r8.speaker: أبو عيسى
TIRMIDHI:3036/r8.claim: Tirmidhi calls the report gharīb: Muhammad b. Salama alone gives it as a connected report, while Yunus b. Bukayr and others transmit it as mursal without Qatada’s father and grandfather.
TIRMIDHI:3036/r8.anchor: قال أبو عيسى هذا حديث غريب لا نعلم أحدا أسنده غير محمد بن سلمة الحراني

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p595#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p595#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p595#2/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās’s account says Ṭuʿma ibn Ubayriq stole Qatāda ibn al-Nuʿmān’s armor in a flour sack, hid it with the Jew Zayd ibn al-Samīn, and was exposed by the flour trail; Banū Ẓafar urged the Prophet to defend Ṭuʿma and blame the Jew, prompting this revelation.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p595#2/r1.anchor: ذكره الثعلبي من رواية أبي صالح عن الكلبي عن ابن عباس ونقله الواحدي في الاسباب عن المفسرين

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p595#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p595#2/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p595#2/r2.claim: Ṭuʿma fled to Mecca, apostatized, and later died when a wall collapsed on him as he broke into a house to steal.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p595#2/r2.anchor: وروي ان طعمة هرب إلى مكة وارتد ونقب حائطا بمكة ليسرق اهله فسقط الحائط عليه فقتله

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p595#3/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p595#3/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p595#3/r1.claim: What God showed the Prophet means what He made him know and revealed to him.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p595#3/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p595#3/r2.speaker: عمر
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p595#3/r2.claim: ʿUmar warns others not to claim their judgments are what God showed them: only the Prophet had divinely guided judgment, while others rely on conjecture and effort.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p595#3/r2.anchor: وعن عمر رضي الله عنه لا يقولن احدكم قضيت بما اراني الله فإن الله لم يجعل ذلك الا لنبيه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p595#3/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p595#3/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p595#3/r3.claim: The Prophet is told not to litigate for traitors against the innocent, specifically not to defend Banū Ẓafar against the Jew.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p595#3/r3.anchor: ولا تكن لأجل الخائنين مخاصما للبراء يعني لا تخاصم اليهود لأجل بني ظفر

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p527#2/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p527#2/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p527#2/r1.claim: The phrase may mean that the Book is true, that it contains truth, or that the Prophet is most entitled to it.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p527#2/r1.anchor: يحتمل ثلاثة أوجه : أحدها : أن الكتاب حق . والثاني : أن فيه ذكر الحق .

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p527#2/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p527#2/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p527#2/r2.claim: Judging by what God showed the Prophet may mean what God taught him was true or what his ijtihad led him to judge true.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p527#2/r2.anchor: يحتمل وجهين : أحدهما : بما أعلمك الله أنه حق . والثاني : بما يؤديك اجتهادك إليه أنه حق .

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p527#2/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p527#2/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p527#2/r3.claim: The prohibition means not to litigate on behalf of traitors.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p527#2/r3.anchor: أي مخاصما عنهم , وهذه الآية نزلت في طعمة بن أبيرق

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p527#2/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p527#2/r4.speaker: السدي
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p527#2/r4.claim: Al-Suddi says Tu'ma ibn Ubayriq had been entrusted with armor and food, denied the deposit, and lacked evidence against him; the Prophet was inclined to defend him before God disclosed the truth.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p527#2/r4.anchor: فقال السدي : كان قد أودع درعا وطعاما فجحده ولم تقم عليه بينة

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p527#2/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p527#2/r5.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p527#2/r5.claim: Al-Hasan says Tu'ma stole armor and food, denied it, planted it in another person's home, and was supported by some Ansar as the Prophet argued or was about to argue for him; the passage proceeds to the clause about accusing an innocent person.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p527#2/r5.anchor: وقال الحسن : إنه كان سرق درعا وطعاما فأنكره واتهم غيره وألقاه في منزله

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p527#2/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p527#2/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p527#2/r6.claim: One account identifies the person involved as a Jew named Yazid ibn al-Samak.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p527#2/r6.anchor: وقيل : إنه كان رجلا من اليهود يقال له يزيد بن السمق

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p527#2/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p527#2/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p527#2/r7.claim: Another account identifies him as an Ansari named Labid ibn Sahl.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p527#2/r7.anchor: وقيل : بل كان رجلا من الأنصار يقال له لبيد بن سهل

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p527#2/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p527#2/r8.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p527#2/r8.claim: Another account identifies him as Tu'ma ibn Ubayriq, who apostatized and fled to Meccan polytheists; the warning in 4:115 was revealed about him.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p527#2/r8.anchor: وقيل : طعمة بن أبيرق فارتد فنزلت فيه هذه الآية

MUQATIL:4:105-108/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:4:105-108/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:4:105-108/r1.claim: Zayd ibn al-Samin entrusted armor to Tuma ibn Ubayriq, who denied it and hid it in Abu Malik’s house; Tuma’s people framed Abu Malik and asked Muhammad to clear Tuma.
MUQATIL:4:105-108/r1.anchor: ثم إن زيدا اليهودى طلب درعه فجحده طعمة، فقال زيد لقومه

MUQATIL:4:105-108/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:4:105-108/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:4:105-108/r2.claim: The Qurʾān was sent down in truth, not in vain; Muhammad should judge by what God taught in scripture. Muqatil links the wording to 34:6.
MUQATIL:4:105-108/r2.anchor: يعنى القرآن { بالحق } لم ننزله باطلا عبثا

MUQATIL:4:105-108/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:4:105-108/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:4:105-108/r3.claim: The traitor for whom Muhammad must not argue is Tuma.

NASAFI-FULL:v1p246#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p246#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p246#2/r1.claim: Ṭuʿma ibn Ubayriq stole armor from his neighbor Qatāda ibn al-Nuʿmān in a flour sack; flour leaked through a hole, and Ṭuʿma hid the armor with the Jew Zayd ibn al-Samīn.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p246#2/r1.anchor: روى أن طعمه بن أبيرق أحد بنى ظفر سرق درعا من جار له اسمه قتادة بن النعمان فى جراب دقيق

NASAFI-FULL:v1p246#2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p246#2/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p246#2/r2.claim: When the armor was traced to the Jew, Ṭuʿma denied it under oath; the Jew said Ṭuʿma had given it to him, supported by Jewish witnesses.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p246#2/r2.anchor: فقال دفعها إلى طعمة وشهد له ناس من اليهود

NASAFI-FULL:v1p246#2/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p246#2/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p246#2/r3.claim: Banū Ẓafar asked the Prophet to argue for their man, fearing his disgrace and the Jew’s acquittal; the Prophet was about to do so when the verse came down.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p246#2/r3.anchor: فسألوه أن يجادل عن صاحبهم وقالوا أن لم تفعل هلك صاحبنا وافتضح

NASAFI-FULL:v1p246#2/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p246#2/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p246#2/r4.anchor: ﴿ إنا أنزلنا إليك الكتاب بالحق ﴾ أى محقا

NASAFI-FULL:v1p246#2/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p246#2/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p246#2/r5.claim: The judgment is according to what God made known and revealed to the Prophet.

NASAFI-FULL:v1p246#2/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p246#2/r6.speaker: أبو منصور
NASAFI-FULL:v1p246#2/r6.claim: Abū Manṣūr says it means what God inspired through reasoning from revealed principles; the verse supports the permissibility of the Prophet’s ijtihād.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p246#2/r6.anchor: بما ألهمك بالنظر فى أصوله المنزلة وفيه دلالة جواز الاجتهاد فى حقه

NASAFI-FULL:v1p246#2/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p246#2/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p246#2/r7.claim: «For the traitors» means on their behalf: the Prophet should not litigate against the Jew for Banū Ẓafar.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p246#2/r7.anchor: ولا تخاصم اليهود لأجل بنى ظفر

BURSEVI:v2p221#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p221#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p221#2/r1.claim: The Book sent in truth is the Qur'an.
BURSEVI:v2p221#2/r1.anchor: {إنآ أنزلنآ إليك الكتاب} أي القرآن إنزالا {بالحق}

BURSEVI:v2p221#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p221#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p221#2/r2.claim: An Ansari, Tu'ma b. Ubayriq, stole his neighbor Qatada b. al-Nu'man's armor, hid it with the Jew Zayd b. al-Samin, and flour leaking from its sack led investigators to the Jew.
BURSEVI:v2p221#2/r2.anchor: روي أن رجلا من الأنصار يقال له طعمة بن أبيرق من بني ظفر سرق درعا من جاره قتادة

BURSEVI:v2p221#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p221#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p221#2/r3.claim: Tu'ma denied the theft and his people urged the Prophet to prosecute the Jew, relying on their apparent testimony; the Prophet withheld judgment for revelation, which exposed Tu'ma and his witnesses as liars and cleared the Jew.
BURSEVI:v2p221#2/r3.anchor: فسألوه أن يجادل اليهودي ليدفع فضيحة البهتان عن صاحبهم طعمة وقالوا له عليه السلام أن يعاقب اليهودي

BURSEVI:v2p221#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p221#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p221#2/r4.claim: Araka means what God made known and revealed to the Prophet; it is not ocular sight or ordinary knowledge, but a recognition called seeing for its force, clarity, and freedom from doubt.
BURSEVI:v2p221#2/r4.anchor: فأراك ليس من الرؤية البصرية ولا من التي بمعنى العلم وإلا لاستدعى ثلاثة مفاعيل بل هو منقول من رأيت بمعنى الاعتقاد والمعرفة

BURSEVI:v2p222/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p222/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p222/r1.claim: Tu'ma's clan knew he had committed the theft, reportedly because he was already a thief in pre-Islamic times, but conspired overnight to blame the Jew and save him from punishment.
BURSEVI:v2p222/r1.anchor: روي أن قومه علموا أن تلك السرقة عمل طعمة بناء على أنه سارق في الجاهلية لكنهم بيتوا طول ليلهم

BURSEVI:v2p222/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p222/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p222/r2.claim: The traitors are Tu'ma and his helpers; being a disputant for them would mean arguing against the innocent Jew on their behalf.
BURSEVI:v2p222/r2.anchor: أي لأجلهم والذب عنهم وهم طعمة ومن يعينه

RAZI-FULL:v11p26/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v11p26/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v11p26/r1.claim: One account of the sequence is that, after detailed discussion of hypocrites and then battle and its rules, the text returns to hypocrites who tried to make the Prophet judge falsely; God exposed them and forbade him to heed them.
RAZI-FULL:v11p26/r1.anchor: لما شرح أحوال المنافقين على سبيل الاستقصاء ثم اتصل بذلك أمر المحاربة ، واتصل بذكر المحاربة ما يتعلق بها من الأحكام الشرعية

RAZI-FULL:v11p26/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v11p26/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v11p26/r2.claim: A second account is that after presenting many laws in this sūra, God affirms that they were revealed by Him and the Messenger may not depart from them to please his people.
RAZI-FULL:v11p26/r2.anchor: لما بين الأحكام الكثيرة في هذه السورة بين أن كل ما عرف بإنزال الله تعالى وأنه ليس للرسول أن يحيد عن شيء منها

RAZI-FULL:v11p26/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v11p26/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v11p26/r3.claim: A third account connects the verse to the command to fight disbelievers: their unbelief does not justify injustice, false accusations, or biased judgment to please hypocrites; judge both sides by revelation.
RAZI-FULL:v11p26/r3.anchor: لما أمر بالمجاهدة مع الكفار بين أن الأمر وإن كان كذلك لكنه لا تجوز الخيانة معهم ولا إلحاق ما لم يفعلوا بهم

RAZI-FULL:v11p26/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v11p26/r4.speaker: المفسرون
RAZI-FULL:v11p26/r4.claim: Commentators agree that most of these verses were revealed about Ṭuʿma ibn Ubayriq; one account says he stole armor, blamed a Jew, and his family asked the Prophet to support their accusation, toward which he leaned before revelation came.
RAZI-FULL:v11p26/r4.anchor: اتفق المفسرون على أن أكثر هذه الآيات نزلت في طعمة بن أبيرق ، ثم في كيفية الواقعة روايات : أحدها : أن طعمة سرق درعا

RAZI-FULL:v11p26/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v11p26/r5.speaker: رواية أخرى
RAZI-FULL:v11p26/r5.claim: A second account says someone entrusted Ṭuʿma with armor without witnesses; when asked to return it, he denied having it.
RAZI-FULL:v11p26/r5.anchor: وثانيها : أن واحدا وضع عنده درعا على سبيل الوديعة ولم يكن هناك شاهد ، فلما طلبها منه جحدها

RAZI-FULL:v11p26/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v11p26/r6.speaker: رواية ثالثة
RAZI-FULL:v11p26/r6.claim: A third account says that when the owner demanded the deposited armor, Ṭuʿma claimed the Jew had stolen it.
RAZI-FULL:v11p26/r6.anchor: وثالثها : أن المودع لما طلب الوديعة زعم أن اليهودي سرق الدرع

RAZI-FULL:v11p26/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v11p26/r7.speaker: العلماء
RAZI-FULL:v11p26/r7.claim: Scholars infer that Ṭuʿma and his people were hypocrites because they asked the Prophet to support a baseless false accusation against the Jew; 4:113 confirms their plot harmed only themselves.
RAZI-FULL:v11p26/r7.anchor: واعلم أن العلماء قالوا هذايدل على أن طعمة وقومه كانوا منافقين ، وإلا لما طلبوا من الرسول نصرة الباطل

RAZI-FULL:v11p26/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v11p26/r8.speaker: روي
RAZI-FULL:v11p26/r8.claim: A report says Ṭuʿma fled to Mecca, apostatized, tried to break through a wall to steal, and was killed when it collapsed on him.
RAZI-FULL:v11p26/r8.anchor: ثم روي أن طعمة هرب إلى مكة وارتد وثقب حائطا هناك لأجل السرقة فسقط الحائط عليه ومات

RAZI-FULL:v11p27/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v11p27/r1.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
RAZI-FULL:v11p27/r1.claim: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī considers three senses of arāka: visual perception is impossible for a judgment; making someone see two things would require a third object; the remaining sense is opinion or knowledge.
RAZI-FULL:v11p27/r1.anchor: قال أبو علي الفارسي : قوله { أراك الله } إما أن يكون منقولا بالهمزة من رأيت التي يراد بها رؤية البصر

RAZI-FULL:v11p27/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v11p27/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v11p27/r2.claim: Here as God showed you means as God made you know: certain knowledge, free of doubt, resembles sight in clarity and force.
RAZI-FULL:v11p27/r2.anchor: ثبت بما قدمنا أن قوله { بما أراك الله } معناه بما أعلمك الله ، وسمي ذلك العلم بالرؤية

RAZI-FULL:v11p27/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v11p27/r3.speaker: عمر
RAZI-FULL:v11p27/r3.claim: ʿUmar says no one should claim to have judged as God showed him, because that designation belongs only to the Prophet; ordinary judgment is conjecture, not certain knowledge.
RAZI-FULL:v11p27/r3.anchor: وكان عمر يقول : لا يقولن أحد قضيت بما أراني الله تعالى لم يجعل ذلك إلا لنبيه

RAZI-FULL:v11p27/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v11p27/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v11p27/r4.claim: The learned authorities infer that the Prophet judged only by revelation and explicit textual proof.
RAZI-FULL:v11p27/r4.anchor: قال المحققون : هذه الآية تدل على أنه عليه الصلاة والسلام ما كان يحكم إلا بالوحي والنص

RAZI-FULL:v11p27/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v11p27/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v11p27/r5.claim: The implication drawn is that the community too must judge only by text, citing the order to follow the Prophet; this would make analogical reasoning forbidden.
RAZI-FULL:v11p27/r5.anchor: وجب أن يكون العمل بالقياس حراما

RAZI-FULL:v11p27/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v11p27/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v11p27/r6.claim: Al-Rāzī answers that once analogy is established as valid, applying it is itself obedience to scripture, which directs people to act on a strong likelihood that an unaddressed case shares the rule of a stated case for a common cause.
RAZI-FULL:v11p27/r6.anchor: والجواب عنه أنه لما قامت الدلالة على أن القياس حجة كان العمل بالقياس عملا بالنص في الحقيقة

RAZI-FULL:v11p27#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v11p27#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v11p27#2/r1.claim: Do not argue on behalf of wrongdoers against the innocent; here, do not defend the hypocrites for Ta'ma.
RAZI-FULL:v11p27#2/r1.anchor: ولا تكن لأجل الخائنين مخاصما لمن كان بريئا عن الذنب

RAZI-FULL:v11p27#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v11p27#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v11p27#2/r2.claim: Ta'ma's people asked the Prophet to defend him and blame the Jew; the Prophet paused for revelation, which exposed Ta'ma as the liar and the Jew as innocent.
RAZI-FULL:v11p27#2/r2.anchor: لما التمسوا من الرسول عليه الصلاة والسلام أن يذب عن طعمة

RAZI-FULL:v11p27#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v11p27#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v11p27#2/r3.claim: The prohibition does not prove the Prophet committed the forbidden act, so the verse does not establish a lapse in prophetic impeccability.

RAZI-FULL:v11p27#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v11p27#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v11p27#2/r4.claim: One answer to the appeal to “seek forgiveness” is that the Prophet may naturally have leaned toward Ta'ma because he appeared to be Muslim; the command addressed that inclination.
RAZI-FULL:v11p27#2/r4.anchor: لعله مال طبعه إلى نصرة طعمة بسبب أنه كان في الظاهر من المسلمين فأمر بالستغفار لهذا القدر

RAZI-FULL:v11p27#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v11p27#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v11p27#2/r5.claim: Alternatively, the Prophet intended to rule from apparently credible testimony, then learned the witnesses had lied; he sought forgiveness for intending a ruling that would have been wrong, though he was excused.
RAZI-FULL:v11p27#2/r5.anchor: ثم لما أطلعه الله تعالى على كذب أولئك الشهود عرف أن ذلك القضاء لو وقع لكان خطأ

RAZI-FULL:v11p27#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v11p27#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v11p27#2/r6.claim: A further reading takes the command to seek forgiveness as a request to seek forgiveness for those who were defending Ta'ma and trying to clear him.
RAZI-FULL:v11p27#2/r6.anchor: استغفر الله لأولئك الذين يذبون عن طعمة ويريدون أن يظهروا براءته
